# ============================================================================
# EXPORT AND DEPLOYMENT UTILITIES
# ============================================================================

class ModelExporter:
    """
    Utility class for exporting quantized models to various formats.
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def export_to_onnx(
        model: nn.Module,
        output_path: str,
        input_shape: Tuple[int, ...] = (1, 3, 32, 32),
        opset_version: int = 11
    ):
        """
        Export model to ONNX format.
        
        Args:
            model: Model to export
            output_path: Path to save ONNX model
            input_shape: Input tensor shape
            opset_version: ONNX opset version
        """
        model.eval()
        dummy_input = torch.randn(input_shape)
        
        try:
            torch.onnx.export(
                model,
                dummy_input,
                output_path,
                export_params=True,
                opset_version=opset_version,
                do_constant_folding=True,
                input_names=['input'],
                output_names=['output'],
                dynamic_axes={
                    'input': {0: 'batch_size'},
                    'output': {0: 'batch_size'}
                }
            )
            print(f"Model exported to ONNX: {output_path}")
            
            # Verify the exported model
            import onnx
            onnx_model = onnx.load(output_path)
            onnx.checker.check_model(onnx_model)
            print("ONNX model verified successfully!")
            
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error exporting to ONNX: {e}")
    
    @staticmethod
    def export_to_torchscript(
        model: nn.Module,
        output_path: str,
        input_shape: Tuple[int, ...] = (1, 3, 32, 32),
        use_trace: bool = True
    ):
        """
        Export model to TorchScript format.
        
        Args:
            model: Model to export
            output_path: Path to save TorchScript model
            input_shape: Input tensor shape
            use_trace: Whether to use tracing (vs scripting)
        """
        model.eval()
        
        try:
            if use_trace:
                dummy_input = torch.randn(input_shape)
                traced_model = torch.jit.trace(model, dummy_input)
            else:
                traced_model = torch.jit.script(model)
            
            traced_model.save(output_path)
            print(f"Model exported to TorchScript: {output_path}")
            
            # Verify
            loaded_model = torch.jit.load(output_path)
            print("TorchScript model verified successfully!")
            
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error exporting to TorchScript: {e}")
    
    @staticmethod
    def export_quantized_weights(
        model: nn.Module,
        output_path: str
    ):
        """
        Export only quantized weights in compact format.
        
        Args:
            model: Model with quantized weights
            output_path: Path to save weights
        """
        quantized_weights = {}
        
        for name, module in model.named_modules():
            if isinstance(module, (QuantizedConv2d, QuantizedLinear)):
                # Get quantized weight
                quantized_weight = QuantizationFunction.apply(
                    module.weight,
                    module.weight_bits,
                    module.weight_min.item(),
                    module.weight_max.item()
                )
                
                quantized_weights[name] = {
                    'weight': quantized_weight.cpu().numpy(),
                    'bits': module.weight_bits,
                    'min': module.weight_min.item(),
                    'max': module.weight_max.item()
                }
                
                if module.bias is not None:
                    quantized_weights[name]['bias'] = module.bias.cpu().numpy()
        
        # Save as compressed numpy archive
        np.savez_compressed(output_path, **quantized_weights)
        
        # Calculate size
        file_size = os.path.getsize(output_path) / (1024 * 1024)
        print(f"Quantized weights exported: {output_path}")
        print(f"File size: {file_size:.2f} MB")


class DeploymentValidator:
    """
    Validator for ensuring model correctness before deployment.
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def validate_numerical_accuracy(
        original_model: nn.Module,
        quantized_model: nn.Module,
        test_loader: torch.utils.data.DataLoader,
        tolerance: float = 0.05
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Validate numerical accuracy between original and quantized models.
        
        Args:
            original_model: Original FP32 model
            quantized_model: Quantized model
            test_loader: Test data loader
            tolerance: Acceptable accuracy difference
            
        Returns:
            Dictionary with validation results
        """
        original_model.eval()
        quantized_model.eval()
        
        original_correct = 0
        quantized_correct = 0
        total = 0
        max_output_diff = 0.0
        
        with torch.no_grad():
            for inputs, targets in test_loader:
                # Original model predictions
                original_outputs = original_model(inputs)
                _, original_pred = original_outputs.max(1)
                original_correct += original_pred.eq(targets).sum().item()
                
                # Quantized model predictions
                quantized_outputs = quantized_model(inputs)
                _, quantized_pred = quantized_outputs.max(1)
                quantized_correct += quantized_pred.eq(targets).sum().item()
                
                # Calculate output difference
                output_diff = (original_outputs - quantized_outputs).abs().max().item()
                max_output_diff = max(max_output_diff, output_diff)
                
                total += targets.size(0)
        
        original_acc = 100. * original_correct / total
        quantized_acc = 100. * quantized_correct / total
        acc_diff = abs(original_acc - quantized_acc)
        
        is_valid = acc_diff <= tolerance
        
        results = {
            'original_accuracy': original_acc,
            'quantized_accuracy': quantized_acc,
            'accuracy_difference': acc_diff,
            'max_output_difference': max_output_diff,
            'is_valid': is_valid,
            'tolerance': tolerance
        }
        
        print("\nNumerical Validation Results:")
        print("-" * 50)
        print(f"Original Model Accuracy: {original_acc:.2f}%")
        print(f"Quantized Model Accuracy: {quantized_acc:.2f}%")
        print(f"Accuracy Difference: {acc_diff:.2f}%")
        print(f"Max Output Difference: {max_output_diff:.6f}")
        print(f"Validation Status: {'✓ PASSED' if is_valid else '✗ FAILED'}")
        print("-" * 50)
        
        return results
    
    @staticmethod
    def validate_inference_speed(
        model: nn.Module,
        input_shape: Tuple[int, ...] = (1, 3, 32, 32),
        min_fps: float = 30.0,
        device: str = 'cuda'
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Validate inference speed meets requirements.
        
        Args:
            model: Model to validate
            input_shape: Input tensor shape
            min_fps: Minimum required FPS
            device: Device to run on
            
        Returns:
            Dictionary with validation results
        """
        benchmark = benchmark_inference(model, input_shape, num_iterations=100, device=device)
        
        is_valid = benchmark['throughput_fps'] >= min_fps
        
        results = {
            'throughput_fps': benchmark['throughput_fps'],
            'min_required_fps': min_fps,
            'is_valid': is_valid
        }
        
        print("\nSpeed Validation Results:")
        print("-" * 50)
        print(f"Measured Throughput: {benchmark['throughput_fps']:.2f} FPS")
        print(f"Required Throughput: {min_fps:.2f} FPS")
        print(f"Validation Status: {'✓ PASSED' if is_valid else '✗ FAILED'}")
        print("-" * 50)
        
        return results
    
    @staticmethod
    def validate_memory_footprint(
        model: nn.Module,
        max_memory_mb: float = 100.0
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Validate model memory footprint.
        
        Args:
            model: Model to validate
            max_memory_mb: Maximum allowed memory in MB
            
        Returns:
            Dictionary with validation results
        """
        # Calculate model size
        param_size = sum(p.numel() * p.element_size() for p in model.parameters())
        buffer_size = sum(b.numel() * b.element_size() for b in model.buffers())
        total_size_mb = (param_size + buffer_size) / (1024 * 1024)
        
        is_valid = total_size_mb <= max_memory_mb
        
        results = {
            'model_size_mb': total_size_mb,
            'max_allowed_mb': max_memory_mb,
            'is_valid': is_valid
        }
        
        print("\nMemory Validation Results:")
        print("-" * 50)
        print(f"Model Size: {total_size_mb:.2f} MB")
        print(f"Maximum Allowed: {max_memory_mb:.2f} MB")
        print(f"Validation Status: {'✓ PASSED' if is_valid else '✗ FAILED'}")
        print("-" * 50)
        
        return results

class QuantizationSearcher:
    """
    Automated search for optimal quantization configuration.
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        model: nn.Module,
        train_loader: torch.utils.data.DataLoader,
        val_loader: torch.utils.data.DataLoader,
        search_space: Dict[str, List[int]]
    ):
        """
        Initialize quantization searcher.
        
        Args:
            model: Base model to quantize
            train_loader: Training data loader
            val_loader: Validation data loader
            search_space: Dictionary mapping layer names to precision options
        """
        self.base_model = model
        self.train_loader = train_loader
        self.val_loader = val_loader
        self.search_space = search_space
        self.search_results = []
    
    def search(
        self,
        num_trials: int = 10,
        epochs_per_trial: int = 5,
        target_metric: str = 'accuracy'
    ) -> Dict[str, int]:
        """
        Perform automated search for optimal quantization.
        
        Args:
            num_trials: Number of configurations to try
            epochs_per_trial: Training epochs per configuration
            target_metric: Metric to optimize ('accuracy' or 'energy')
            
        Returns:
            Best quantization configuration found
        """
        print("\n" + "=" * 70)
        print("AUTOMATED QUANTIZATION SEARCH")
        print("=" * 70)
        print(f"\nSearch Parameters:")
        print(f"  Trials: {num_trials}")
        print(f"  Epochs per trial: {epochs_per_trial}")
        print(f"  Target metric: {target_metric}")
        print("=" * 70 + "\n")
        
        best_config = None
        best_score = 0.0 if target_metric == 'accuracy' else float('inf')
        
        for trial in range(num_trials):
            print(f"\nTrial {trial + 1}/{num_trials}")
            print("-" * 70)
            
            # Generate random configuration
            config = self._generate_config()
            print(f"Configuration: {config}")
            
            # Create and train model with this configuration
            model = self._create_model_with_config(config)
            
            # Quick training
            final_acc, avg_energy = self._quick_train(model, epochs_per_trial)
            
            # Calculate score
            if target_metric == 'accuracy':
                score = final_acc
                is_better = score > best_score
            else:  # energy
                score = avg_energy
                is_better = score < best_score
            
            # Store results
            self.search_results.append({
                'config': config,
                'accuracy': final_acc,
                'energy': avg_energy,
                'score': score
            })
            
            print(f"Accuracy: {final_acc:.2f}%, Energy: {avg_energy:.4f}")
            
            # Update best
            if is_better:
                best_score = score
                best_config = config
                print("✓ New best configuration!")
        
        print("\n" + "=" * 70)
        print("SEARCH COMPLETED")
        print("=" * 70)
        print(f"\nBest Configuration:")
        for layer, bits in best_config.items():
            print(f"  {layer}: {bits}-bit")
        print(f"\nBest {target_metric}: {best_score:.4f}")
        print("=" * 70 + "\n")
        
        return best_config
    
    def _generate_config(self) -> Dict[str, int]:
        """Generate random quantization configuration."""
        config = {}
        for layer_name, options in self.search_space.items():
            config[layer_name] = np.random.choice(options)
        return config
    
    def _create_model_with_config(self, config: Dict[str, int]) -> nn.Module:
        """Create model with given quantization configuration."""
        # Create precision config for MixedPrecisionNet
        precision_config = {
            layer: (bits, bits) for layer, bits in config.items()
        }
        return MixedPrecisionNet(num_classes=10, precision_config=precision_config)
    
    def _quick_train(self, model: nn.Module, epochs: int) -> Tuple[float, float]:
        """Quickly train model and return final accuracy and average energy."""
        device = 'cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu'
        model.to(device)
        
        optimizer = optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=0.001)
        criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
        
        total_energy = 0.0
        
        for epoch in range(epochs):
            model.train()
            for inputs, targets in self.train_loader:
                inputs, targets = inputs.to(device), targets.to(device)
                
                optimizer.zero_grad()
                outputs = model(inputs)
                loss = criterion(outputs, targets)
                loss.backward()
                optimizer.step()
        
        # Evaluate
        model.eval()
        correct = 0
        total = 0
        
        with torch.no_grad():
            for inputs, targets in self.val_loader:
                inputs, targets = inputs.to(device), targets.to(device)
                outputs = model(inputs)
                _,

        # Estimate energy (simplified)
        avg_precision = np.mean([info['precision'] for info in

        avg_energy = (avg_precision / 32) ** 2
        
        return final_acc, avg_energy

        """
        Visualize search results.
        
        Args:
            save_path: Optional path to save figure
        """
        if not self.search_results:

        axes[0].grid(True, alpha=0.3)
        
        # Plot 2: Accuracy vs Energy trade-off
        axes[1].scatter(energies, accuracies, s=100, alpha=0.6)
        axes[1].set_xlabel('Energy Consumption')
        axes[1].set_ylabel('Accuracy (%)')
        axes[1].set_title('Accuracy vs Energy Trade-off')
        axes[1].grid(True, alpha=0.3)
        
        # Annotate best points
        best_acc_idx = np.argmax(accuracies)
        best_energy_idx = np.argmin(energies)
        
        axes[1].scatter(energies[best_acc_idx], accuracies[best_acc_idx], 
                       s=200, color='red', marker='*', label='Best Accuracy')
        axes[1].scatter(energies[best_energy_idx], accuracies[best_energy_idx], 
                       s=200, color='green', marker='*', label='Best Energy')
        axes[1].legend()
        
        plt.tight_layout()
        
        if save_path:
            plt.savefig(save_path, dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
            print(f"Search results visualization saved to {save_path}")
        else:
            plt.show()


# ============================================================================
# KNOWLEDGE DISTILLATION FOR QUANTIZED MODELS
# ============================================================================

class QuantizationDistiller:
    """
    Knowledge distillation to improve quantized model accuracy.
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        teacher_model: nn.Module,
        student_model: nn.Module,
        temperature: float = 3.0,
        alpha: float = 0.5
    ):
        """
        Initialize distillation trainer.
        
        Args:
            teacher_model: Full-precision teacher model
            student_model: Quantized student model
            temperature: Temperature for softening predictions
            alpha: Weight for distillation loss (1-alpha for hard labels)
        """
        self.teacher = teacher_model
        self.student = student_model
        self.temperature = temperature
        self.alpha = alpha
        
        self.teacher.eval()  # Teacher is always in eval mode
    
    def distillation_loss(
        self,
        student_outputs: torch.Tensor,
        teacher_outputs: torch.Tensor,
        targets: torch.Tensor,
        criterion: nn.Module
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Calculate combined distillation loss.
        
        Args:
            student_outputs: Student model outputs
            teacher_outputs: Teacher model outputs
            targets: Ground truth labels
            criterion: Base loss criterion
            
        Returns:
            Combined loss
        """
        # Hard label loss
        hard_loss = criterion(student_outputs, targets)
        
        # Soft label loss (KL divergence)
        soft_student = F.log_softmax(student_outputs / self.temperature, dim=1)
        soft_teacher = F.softmax(teacher_outputs / self.temperature, dim=1)
        soft_loss = F.kl_div(soft_student, soft_teacher, reduction='batchmean')
        soft_loss = soft_loss * (self.temperature ** 2)
        
        # Combined loss
        total_loss = self.alpha * soft_loss + (1 - self.alpha) * hard_loss
        
        return total_loss
    
    def train_with_distillation(
        self,
        train_loader: torch.utils.data.DataLoader,
        val_loader: torch.utils.data.DataLoader,
        num_epochs: int = 10,
        learning_rate: float = 0.001,
        device: str = 'cuda'
    ):
        """
        Train student model with knowledge distillation.
        
        Args:
            train_loader: Training data loader
            val_loader: Validation data loader
            num_epochs: Number of training epochs
            learning_rate: Learning rate
            device: Device to train on
        """
        self.teacher.to(device)
        self.student.to(device)
        
        optimizer = optim.Adam(self.student.parameters(), lr=learning_rate)
        criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
        
        print("\n" + "=" * 70)
        print("KNOWLEDGE DISTILLATION TRAINING")
        print("=" * 70)
        print(f"\nConfiguration:")
        print(f"  Temperature: {self.temperature}")
        print(f"  Alpha (distillation weight): {self.alpha}")
        print(f"  Epochs: {num_epochs}")
        print(f"  Learning Rate: {learning_rate}")
        print("=" * 70 + "\n")
        
        best_val_acc = 0.0
        
        for epoch in range(num_epochs):
            # Training
            self.student.train()
            train_loss = 0.0
            train_correct = 0
            train_total = 0
            
            for inputs, targets in train_loader:
                inputs, targets = inputs.to(device), targets.to(device)
                
                # Get teacher predictions (no gradient)
                with torch.no_grad():
                    teacher_outputs = self.teacher(inputs)
                
                # Get student predictions
                optimizer.zero_grad()
                student_outputs = self.student(inputs)
                
                # Calculate distillation loss
                loss = self.distillation_loss(
                    student_outputs, teacher_outputs, targets, criterion
                )
                
                loss.backward()
                optimizer.step()
                
                train_loss += loss.item()
                _, predicted = student_outputs.max(1)
                train_total += targets.size(0)
                train_correct += predicted.eq(targets).sum().item()
            
            train_acc = 100. * train_correct / train_total
            avg_train_loss = train_loss / len(train_loader)
            
            # Validation
            self.student.eval()
            val_loss = 0.0
            val_correct = 0
            val_total = 0
            
            with torch.no_grad():
                for inputs, targets in val_loader:
                    inputs, targets = inputs.to(device), targets.to(device)
                    
                    outputs = self.student(inputs)
                    loss = criterion(outputs, targets)
                    
                    val_loss += loss.item()
                    _, predicted = outputs.max(1)
                    val_total += targets.size(0)
                    val_correct += predicted.eq(targets).sum().item()
            
            val_acc = 100. * val_correct / val_total
            avg_val_loss = val_loss / len(val_loader)
            
            # Print progress
            print(f"Epoch {epoch+1}/{num_epochs}")
            print(f"  Train - Loss: {avg_train_loss:.4f}, Acc: {train_acc:.2f}%")
            print(f"  Val   - Loss: {avg_val_loss:.4f}, Acc: {val_acc:.2f}%")
            
            if val_acc > best_val_acc:
                best_val_acc = val_acc
                print(f"  ✓ New best validation accuracy!")
            print()
        
        print("=" * 70)
        print(f"Distillation training completed!")
        print(f"Best validation accuracy: {best_val_acc:.2f}%")
        print("=" * 70 + "\n")


# ============================================================================
# PROGRESSIVE QUANTIZATION STRATEGY
# ============================================================================

class ProgressiveQuantizer:
    """
    Progressive quantization that gradually reduces precision during training.
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        model: nn.Module,
        initial_bits: int = 32,
        target_bits: int = 4,
        num_stages: int = 4
    ):
        """
        Initialize progressive quantizer.
        
        Args:
            model: Model to quantize progressively
            initial_bits: Starting precision
            target_bits: Final target precision
            num_stages: Number of quantization stages
        """
        self.model = model
        self.initial_bits = initial_bits
        self.target_bits = target_bits
        self.num_stages = num_stages
        
        # Calculate precision schedule
        self.precision_schedule = self._create_schedule()
    
    def _create_schedule(self) -> List[int]:
        """Create precision reduction schedule."""
        schedule = []
        
        # Exponential decay from initial to target
        for stage in range(self.num_stages):
            progress = stage / (self.num_stages - 1)
            
            # Logarithmic interpolation
            log_initial = np.log2(self.initial_bits)
            log_target = np.log2(self.target_bits)
            log_current = log_initial + progress * (log_target - log_initial)
            
            current_bits = 2 ** round(log_current)
            schedule.append(int(current_bits))
        
        return schedule
    
    def train_progressive(
        self,
        train_loader: torch.utils.data.DataLoader,
        val_loader: torch.utils.data.DataLoader,
        epochs_per_stage: int = 5,
        learning_rate: float = 0.001,
        device: str = 'cuda'
    ):
        """
        Train with progressive quantization.
        
        Args:
            train_loader: Training data loader
            val_loader: Validation data loader
            epochs_per_stage: Training epochs per quantization stage
            learning_rate: Learning rate
            device: Device to train on
        """
        self.model.to(device)
        
        print("\n" + "=" * 70)
        print("PROGRESSIVE QUANTIZATION TRAINING")
        print("=" * 70)
        print(f"\nPrecision Schedule: {self.precision_schedule}")
        print(f"Epochs per stage: {epochs_per_stage}")
        print("=" * 70 + "\n")
        
        optimizer = optim.Adam(self.model.parameters(), lr=learning_rate)
        criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
        
        stage_results = []
        
        for stage, precision in enumerate(self.precision_schedule):
            print(f"\nStage {stage+1}/{self.num_stages} - {precision}-bit precision")
            print("-" * 70)
            
            # Update model precision
            self._update_model_precision(precision)
            
            # Train for this stage
            for epoch in range(epochs_per_stage):
                # Training
                self.model.train()
                train_loss = 0.0
                
                for inputs, targets in train_loader:
                    inputs, targets = inputs.to(device), targets.to(device)
                    
                    optimizer.zero_grad()
                    outputs = self.model(inputs)
                    loss = criterion(outputs, targets)
                    loss.backward()
                    optimizer.step()
                    
                    train_loss += loss.item()
                
                avg_loss = train_loss / len(train_loader)
                
                # Validation
                val_acc = self._validate(val_loader, device)
                
                print(f"  Epoch {epoch+1}/{epochs_per_stage} - "
                      f"Loss: {avg_loss:.4f}, Val Acc: {val_acc:.2f}%")
            
            # Store stage results
            final_val_acc = self._validate(val_loader, device)
            stage_results.append({
                'stage': stage + 1,
                'precision': precision,
                'val_accuracy': final_val_acc
            })
            
            print(f"Stage {stage+1} completed - Final Val Acc: {final_val_acc:.2f}%\n")
        
        # Print summary
        print("=" * 70)
        print("PROGRESSIVE QUANTIZATION SUMMARY")
        print("=" * 70)
        print(f"\n{'Stage':<10} {'Precision':<15} {'Val Accuracy':<15}")
        print("-" * 70)
        
        for result in stage_results:
            print(f"{result['stage']:<10} {result['precision']:<15} "
                  f"{result['val_accuracy']:<15.2f}%")
        
        print("\n" + "=" * 70 + "\n")
    
    def _update_model_precision(self, precision: int):
        """Update precision for all quantized layers."""
        for module in self.model.modules():
            if isinstance(module, (QuantizedConv2d, QuantizedLinear)):
                module.weight_bits = precision
                module.activation_bits = precision
    
    def _validate(self, val_loader: torch.utils.data.DataLoader, device: str) -> float:
        """Validate model and return accuracy."""
        self.model.eval()
        correct = 0
        total = 0
        
        with torch.no_grad():
            for inputs, targets in val_loader:
                inputs, targets = inputs.to(device), targets.to(device)
                outputs = self.model(inputs)
                _, predicted = outputs.max(1)
                total += targets.size(0)
                correct += predicted.eq(targets).sum().item()
        
        return 100. * correct / total

  • Check for proper batch size configuration
  • Profile to identify bottlenecks
  • Consider layer fusion and operator optimization

Issue: Memory overflow on target device

  • Reduce model size with more aggressive quantization
  • Apply pruning before quantization
  • Use model partitioning for large models
  • Optimize activation memory with checkpointing

Issue: Inconsistent results across runs

  • Use deterministic algorithms
  • Validate quantization ranges are properly calibrated
  • Check for numerical instabilities

    print("-" * 70)
    
    from torch.utils.data import TensorDataset, DataLoader
    
    # Synthetic dataset for demonstration
    X_train = torch.randn(1000, 3, 32, 32)
    y_train = torch.randint(0, 10, (1000,))
    X_val = torch.randn(200, 3, 32, 32)
    y_val = torch.randint(0, 10, (200,))
    X_test = torch.randn(200, 3, 32, 32)
    y_test = torch.randint(0, 10, (200,))
    
    train_dataset = TensorDataset(X_train, y_train)
    val_dataset = TensorDataset(X_val, y_val)
    test_dataset = TensorDataset(X_test, y_test)
    
    train_loader = DataLoader(train_dataset, batch_size=32, shuffle=True)
    val_loader = DataLoader(val_dataset, batch_size=32)
    test_loader = DataLoader(test_dataset, batch_size=32)
    
    print(f"Training samples: {len(train_dataset)}")
    print(f"Validation samples: {len(val_dataset)}")
    print(f"Test samples: {len(test_dataset)}")
    print("✓ Data preparation complete\n")
    
    # Step 2: Train baseline model
    print("Step 2: Train Baseline (FP32) Model")
    print("-" * 70)
    
    baseline_model = SimpleConvNet(num_classes=10)
    device = 'cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu'
    
    baseline_trainer = LowPrecisionTrainer(baseline_model, device=device, use_amp=False)
    optimizer_baseline = optim.Adam(baseline_model.parameters(), lr=0.001)
    criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
    
    # Quick training
    for epoch in range(3):
        for inputs, targets in train_loader:
            inputs, targets = inputs.to(device), targets.to(device)
            loss, _ = baseline_trainer.train_step(inputs, targets, optimizer_baseline, criterion)
    
    baseline_loss, baseline_acc = baseline_trainer.evaluate(val_loader, criterion)
    print(f"Baseline Model - Val Loss: {baseline_loss:.4f}, Val Acc: {baseline_acc:.2f}%")
    print("✓ Baseline training complete\n")
    
    # Step 3: Create and train quantized model
    print("Step 3: Train Quantized Model (Mixed-Precision)")
    print("-" * 70)
    
    quantized_config = {
        'conv1': (8, 8),
        'conv2': (4, 4),
        'conv3': (4, 4),
        'conv4': (4, 4),
        'fc1': (4, 4),
        'fc2': (8, 8),
    }
    
    quantized_model = MixedPrecisionNet(num_classes=10, precision_config=quantized_config)
    
    # Train with unified pipeline
    unified_config = {
        'device': device,
        'use_amp': True,
        'use_qat': False,
        'use_dynamic_precision': False,
        'total_epochs': 5
    }
    
    unified_trainer = UnifiedEnergyEfficientTrainer(quantized_model, unified_config)
    unified_trainer.train(train_loader, val_loader, num_epochs=5, learning_rate=0.001)
    
    print("✓ Quantized model training complete\n")
    
    # Step 4: Knowledge Distillation (optional refinement)
    print("Step 4: Knowledge Distillation Refinement")
    print("-" * 70)
    
    distiller = QuantizationDistiller(
        teacher_model=baseline_model,
        student_model=quantized_model,
        temperature=3.0,
        alpha=0.7
    )
    
    distiller.train_with_distillation(
        train_loader=train_loader,
        val_loader=val_loader,
        num_epochs=3,
        learning_rate=0.0001,
        device=device
    )
    
    print("✓ Knowledge distillation complete\n")
    
    # Step 5: Validation
    print("Step 5: Deployment Validation")
    print("-" * 70)
    
    validator = DeploymentValidator()
    
    # Numerical accuracy
    numerical_results = validator.validate_numerical_accuracy(
        baseline_model,
        quantized_model,
        test_loader,
        tolerance=5.0
    )
    
    # Inference speed
    speed_results = validator.validate_inference_speed(
        quantized_model,
        min_fps=30.0,
        device=device
    )
    
    # Memory footprint
    memory_results = validator.validate_memory_footprint(
        quantized_model,
        max_memory_mb=100.0
    )
    
    all_passed = (
        numerical_results['is_valid'] and
        speed_results['is_valid'] and
        memory_results['is_valid']
    )
    
    print(f"\n{'✓' if all_passed else '✗'} All validation checks {'PASSED' if all_passed else 'FAILED'}\n")
    
    # Step 6: Model Analysis
    print("Step 6: Comprehensive Model Analysis")
    print("-" * 70)
    
    analyzer = ModelCompressionAnalyzer()
    analysis = analyzer.analyze_model(quantized_model, "Optimized Model")
    analyzer.print_analysis(analysis)
    
    # Step 7: Export for Deployment
    print("Step 7: Export for Deployment")
    print("-" * 70)
    
    exporter = ModelExporter()
    
    # Save PyTorch model
    save_quantized_model(
        quantized_model,
        "production_model.pth",
        config=quantized_config
    )
    
    # Export to TorchScript
    exporter.export_to_torchscript(
        quantized_model,
        "production_model.pt",
        use_trace=True
    )
    
    # Export quantized weights
    exporter.export_quantized_weights(
        quantized_model,
        "production_weights.npz"
    )
    
    print("✓ Model export complete\n")
    
    # Step 8: Generate Deployment Configuration
    print("Step 8: Generate Deployment Configuration")
    print("-" * 70)
    
    guide = ProductionDeploymentGuide()
    guide.generate_deployment_config(
        model_name="EfficientImageClassifier",

        target_hardware="GPU_NVIDIA_T4",

    )
    
    print("\n✓ Deployment configuration generated\n")
    
    # Step 9: Benchmark
    print("Step 9: Final Benchmarking")
    print("-" * 70)
    
    models_to_compare = {
        'Baseline (FP32)': baseline_model,
        'Quantized (Mixed-Precision)': quantized_model
    }
    
    compare_model_variants(models_to_compare)
    
    # Final Summary
    print("\n" + "=" * 70)
    print("END-TO-END PIPELINE COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!")
    print("=" * 70)
    print("\nSummary:")
    print(f"  • Baseline Accuracy: {baseline_acc:.2f}%")
    print(f"  • Quantized Accuracy: {numerical_results['quantized_accuracy']:.2f}%")
    print(f"  • Accuracy Loss: {numerical_results['accuracy_difference']:.2f}%")
    print(f"  • Model Compression: {analysis['compression_ratio']:.2f}x")
    print(f"  • Inference Speedup: {analysis['theoretical_speedup']:.2f}x")
    print(f"  • Memory Footprint: {memory_results['model_size_mb']:.2f} MB")
    print(f"  • Throughput: {speed_results['throughput_fps']:.2f} FPS")

### **Troubleshooting:**

**Q: CUDA out of memory?**
A: Reduce batch size or use gradient accumulation

**Q: Accuracy drops too much?**
A: Use knowledge distillation or progressive quantization

**Q: Slow inference?**
A: Enable hardware optimizations, check batch size

**Q: Model too large?**
A: Use more aggressive quantization (ternary/binary)

### **Contributing & Extending:**

To add a new quantization pattern:

```python
class MyCustomQuantization(torch.autograd.Function):
    @staticmethod
    def forward(ctx, input, num_bits):
        # Your quantization logic
        return quantized_input
    
    @staticmethod
    def backward(ctx, grad_output):
        # Gradient handling
        return grad_output, None

class CustomQuantizedLayer(nn.Module):
    def forward(self, x):
        return MyCustomQuantization.apply(x, self.bits)
```

# ============================================================================
# ADDITIONAL UTILITIES AND HELPER FUNCTIONS
# ============================================================================

class PerformanceMonitor:
    """
    Real-time performance monitoring for deployed models.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, model_name: str = "model"):
        """
        Initialize performance monitor.
        
        Args:
            model_name: Name of the model being monitored
        """
        self.model_name = model_name
        self.metrics = {
            'inference_times': [],
            'batch_sizes': [],
            'memory_usage': [],
            'timestamps': []
        }
        self.start_time = time.time()
    
    def log_inference(
        self,
        inference_time: float,
        batch_size: int,
        memory_mb: Optional[float] = None
    ):
        """
        Log a single inference.
        
        Args:
            inference_time: Time taken for inference (seconds)
            batch_size: Batch size used
            memory_mb: Memory usage in MB (optional)
        """
        self.metrics['inference_times'].append(inference_time)
        self.metrics['batch_sizes'].append(batch_size)
        self.metrics['timestamps'].append(time.time() - self.start_time)
        
        if memory_mb is not None:
            self.metrics['memory_usage'].append(memory_mb)
    
    def get_statistics(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Get performance statistics.
        
        Returns:
            Dictionary containing performance metrics
        """
        if not self.metrics['inference_times']:
            return {}
        
        times = np.array(self.metrics['inference_times'])
        
        stats = {
            'total_inferences': len(times),
            'avg_inference_time_ms': np.mean(times) * 1000,
            'p50_inference_time_ms': np.percentile(times, 50) * 1000,
            'p95_inference_time_ms': np.percentile(times, 95) * 1000,
            'p99_inference_time_ms': np.percentile(times, 99) * 1000,
            'min_inference_time_ms': np.min(times) * 1000,
            'max_inference_time_ms': np.max(times) * 1000,
            'throughput_qps': len(times) / (time.time() - self.start_time)
        }
        
        if self.metrics['memory_usage']:
            mem = np.array(self.metrics['memory_usage'])
            stats.update({
                'avg_memory_mb': np.mean(mem),
                'max_memory_mb': np.max(mem)
            })
        
        return stats
    
    def print_report(self):
        """Print performance report."""
        stats = self.get_statistics()
        
        if not stats:
            print("No performance data collected yet.")
            return
        
        print("\n" + "=" * 70)
        print(f"PERFORMANCE REPORT: {self.model_name}")
        print("=" * 70)
        print(f"\nTotal Inferences: {stats['total_inferences']:,}")
        print(f"Throughput: {stats['throughput_qps']:.2f} queries/sec")
        print(f"\nLatency Statistics (ms):")
        print(f"  Average: {stats['avg_inference_time_ms']:.2f}")
        print(f"  P50:     {stats['p50_inference_time_ms']:.2f}")
        print(f"  P95:     {stats['p95_inference_time_ms']:.2f}")
        print(f"  P99:     {stats['p99_inference_time_ms']:.2f}")
        print(f"  Min:     {stats['min_inference_time_ms']:.2f}")
        print(f"  Max:     {stats['max_inference_time_ms']:.2f}")
        
        if 'avg_memory_mb' in stats:
            print(f"\nMemory Usage:")
            print(f"  Average: {stats['avg_memory_mb']:.2f} MB")
            print(f"  Peak:    {stats['max_memory_mb']:.2f} MB")
        
        print("=" * 70 + "\n")
    
    def export_metrics(self, filepath: str):
        """
        Export metrics to JSON file.
        
        Args:
            filepath: Path to save metrics
        """
        with open(filepath, 'w') as f:
            json.dump({
                'model_name': self.model_name,
                'statistics': self.get_statistics(),
                'raw_metrics': {
                    k: [float(v) for v in vals] 
                    for k, vals in self.metrics.items()
                }
            }, f, indent=2)
        
        print(f"Metrics exported to: {filepath}")


class BatchProcessor:
    """
    Efficient batch processing for inference.
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        model: nn.Module,
        batch_size: int = 32,
        device: str = 'cuda'
    ):
        """
        Initialize batch processor.
        
        Args:
            model: Model for inference
            batch_size: Batch size for processing
            device: Device to run on
        """
        self.model = model
        self.batch_size = batch_size
        self.device = device
        
        self.model.to(device)
        self.model.eval()
        
        self.monitor = PerformanceMonitor(model.__class__.__name__)
    
    def process_dataset(
        self,
        dataset: torch.utils.data.Dataset,
        num_workers: int = 4
    ) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, Dict[str, Any]]:
        """
        Process entire dataset efficiently.
        
        Args:
            dataset: Dataset to process
            num_workers: Number of data loading workers
            
        Returns:
            Tuple of (predictions, statistics)
        """
        loader = torch.utils.data.DataLoader(
            dataset,
            batch_size=self.batch_size,
            shuffle=False,
            num_workers=num_workers,
            pin_memory=True if self.device == 'cuda' else False
        )
        
        all_predictions = []
        
        with torch.no_grad():
            for batch in loader:
                if isinstance(batch, (list, tuple)):
                    inputs = batch[0]
                else:
                    inputs = batch
                
                inputs = inputs.to(self.device)
                
                start_time = time.time()
                outputs = self.model(inputs)
                inference_time = time.time() - start_time
                
                # Log performance
                self.monitor.log_inference(
                    inference_time,
                    inputs.size(0)
                )
                
                # Get predictions
                _, predictions = outputs.max(1)
                all_predictions.append(predictions.cpu().numpy())
        
        # Combine all predictions
        all_predictions = np.concatenate(all_predictions)
        
        # Get statistics
        stats = self.monitor.get_statistics()
        
        return all_predictions, stats
    
    def process_single(self, input_tensor: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Process single input with performance monitoring.
        
        Args:
            input_tensor: Input tensor
            
        Returns:
            Output tensor
        """
        input_tensor = input_tensor.to(self.device)
        
        start_time = time.time()
        with torch.no_grad():
            output = self.model(input_tensor)
        inference_time = time.time() - start_time
        
        self.monitor.log_inference(inference_time, input_tensor.size(0))
        
        return output


class ModelPruner:
    """
    Prune models to further reduce size and improve efficiency.
    Combines well with quantization for maximum compression.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, model: nn.Module):
        """
        Initialize model pruner.
        
        Args:
            model: Model to prune
        """
        self.model = model
    
    def magnitude_prune(
        self,
        amount: float = 0.3,
        layers_to_prune: Optional[List[str]] = None
    ):
        """
        Apply magnitude-based pruning.
        
        Args:
            amount: Fraction of weights to prune (0-1)
            layers_to_prune: List of layer names to prune (None = all)
        """
        import torch.nn.utils.prune as prune
        
        print(f"\nApplying magnitude pruning (amount={amount})...")
        
        pruned_count = 0
        total_params = 0
        
        for name, module in self.model.named_modules():
            if isinstance(module, (nn.Conv2d, nn.Linear)):
                if layers_to_prune is None or name in layers_to_prune:
                    prune.l1_unstructured(module, name='weight', amount=amount)
                    pruned_count += 1
                    total_params += module.weight.numel()
        
        print(f"Pruned {pruned_count} layers")
        print(f"Total parameters affected: {total_params:,}")
        print(f"Theoretical sparsity: {amount * 100:.1f}%")
    
    def structured_prune(
        self,
        amount: float = 0.3,
        dim: int = 0
    ):
        """
        Apply structured pruning (removes entire filters/neurons).
        
        Args:
            amount: Fraction of structures to prune
            dim: Dimension to prune along (0=filters, 1=channels)
        """
        import torch.nn.utils.prune as prune
        
        print(f"\nApplying structured pruning (amount={amount}, dim={dim})...")
        
        for name, module in self.model.named_modules():
            if isinstance(module, nn.Conv2d):
                prune.ln_structured(
                    module,
                    name='weight',
                    amount=amount,
                    n=2,
                    dim=dim
                )
        
        print("Structured pruning applied")
    
    def get_sparsity(self) -> Dict[str, float]:
        """
        Calculate actual sparsity for each layer.
        
        Returns:
            Dictionary mapping layer names to sparsity ratios
        """
        sparsity_info = {}
        
        for name, module in self.model.named_modules():
            if isinstance(module, (nn.Conv2d, nn.Linear)):
                if hasattr(module, 'weight'):
                    weight = module.weight
                    zeros = (weight == 0).sum().item()
                    total = weight.numel()
                    sparsity = zeros / total
                    sparsity_info[name] = sparsity
        
        return sparsity_info
    
    def print_sparsity_report(self):
        """Print sparsity report for all layers."""
        sparsity = self.get_sparsity()
        
        print("\n" + "=" * 70)
        print("SPARSITY REPORT")
        print("=" * 70)
        print(f"\n{'Layer':<30} {'Sparsity':<15} {'Parameters':<15}")
        print("-" * 70)
        
        total_params = 0
        total_zeros = 0
        
        for name, module in self.model.named_modules():
            if name in sparsity:
                params = module.weight.numel()
                zeros = int(sparsity[name] * params)
                
                total_params += params
                total_zeros += zeros
                
                print(f"{name:<30} {sparsity[name]*100:>6.2f}% {params:>15,}")
        
        overall_sparsity = total_zeros / total_params if total_params > 0 else 0
        
        print("-" * 70)
        print(f"{'Overall':<30} {overall_sparsity*100:>6.2f}% {total_params:>15,}")
        print("=" * 70 + "\n")


class EnergyEstimator:
    """
    Estimate energy consumption for different model configurations.
    """
    
    # Energy coefficients (relative to FP32 = 1.0)
    ENERGY_COEFFICIENTS = {
        32: 1.0,    # FP32 baseline
        16: 0.5,    # FP16
        8: 0.25,    # INT8
        4: 0.125,   # INT4
        2: 0.0625,  # INT2
        1: 0.03125  # Binary
    }
    
    @staticmethod
    def estimate_layer_energy(
        layer: nn.Module,
        input_shape: Tuple[int, ...],
        precision: int = 32
    ) -> float:
        """
        Estimate energy for a single layer.
        
        Args:
            layer: Layer to analyze
            input_shape: Input tensor shape
            precision: Bit-width used
            
        Returns:
            Estimated energy (arbitrary units)
        """
        # Calculate number of operations
        if isinstance(layer, nn.Conv2d):
            # Conv2d: batch * out_h * out_w * out_c * k_h * k_w * in_c
            batch, in_c, in_h, in_w = input_shape
            k_h, k_w = layer.kernel_size
            out_c = layer.out_channels
            
            # Calculate output dimensions
            out_h = (in_h + 2 * layer.padding[0] - k_h) // layer.stride[0] + 1
            out_w = (in_w + 2 * layer.padding[1] - k_w) // layer.stride[1] + 1
            
            ops = batch * out_h * out_w * out_c * k_h * k_w * in_c
            
        elif isinstance(layer, nn.Linear):
            # Linear: batch * in_features * out_features
            batch = input_shape[0]
            ops = batch * layer.in_features * layer.out_features
            
        else:
            return 0.0
        
        # Energy = operations * precision_factor
        precision_factor = EnergyEstimator.ENERGY_COEFFICIENTS.get(precision, 1.0)
        energy = ops * precision_factor
        
        return energy
    
    @staticmethod
    def estimate_model_energy(
        model: nn.Module,
        input_shape: Tuple[int, ...] = (1, 3, 32, 32)
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Estimate total energy for model.
        
        Args:
            model: Model to analyze
            input_shape: Input tensor shape
            
        Returns:
            Dictionary with energy estimates
        """
        total_energy = 0.0
        layer_energies = {}
        
        # Get precision for each layer
        for name, module in model.named_modules():
            if isinstance(module, (nn.Conv2d, nn.Linear)):
                # Determine precision
                if isinstance(module, (QuantizedConv2d, QuantizedLinear)):
                    precision = module.weight_bits
                elif isinstance(module, (BinaryConv2d, BinaryLinear)):
                    precision = 1
                else:
                    precision = 32
                
                # Estimate energy (simplified - would need actual forward pass for exact shapes)
                energy = EnergyEstimator.estimate_layer_energy(
                    module,
                    input_shape,
                    precision
                )
                
                layer_energies[name] =
```python
                layer_energies[name] = {
                    'energy': energy,
                    'precision': precision
                }
                total_energy += energy
        
        # Calculate average precision
        precisions = [info['precision'] for info in layer_energies.values()]
        avg_precision = np.mean(precisions) if precisions else 32
        
        # Compare to FP32 baseline
        baseline_energy = sum(
            info['energy'] / EnergyEstimator.ENERGY_COEFFICIENTS[info['precision']]
            for info in layer_energies.values()
        )
        
        energy_savings = (1 - total_energy / baseline_energy) * 100 if baseline_energy > 0 else 0
        
        return {
            'total_energy': total_energy,
            'baseline_energy': baseline_energy,
            'energy_savings_percent': energy_savings,
            'avg_precision': avg_precision,
            'layer_energies': layer_energies
        }
    
    @staticmethod
    def print_energy_report(energy_info: Dict[str, Any]):
        """
        Print formatted energy report.
        
        Args:
            energy_info: Energy information from estimate_model_energy
        """
        print("\n" + "=" * 70)
        print("ENERGY CONSUMPTION REPORT")
        print("=" * 70)
        
        print(f"\nOverall Statistics:")
        print(f"  Total Energy: {energy_info['total_energy']:.2e} units")
        print(f"  Baseline (FP32): {energy_info['baseline_energy']:.2e} units")
        print(f"  Energy Savings: {energy_info['energy_savings_percent']:.1f}%")
        print(f"  Average Precision: {energy_info['avg_precision']:.1f}-bit")
        
        print(f"\nPer-Layer Breakdown:")
        print(f"{'Layer':<30} {'Energy':<15} {'Precision':<12}")
        print("-" * 70)
        
        for name, info in energy_info['layer_energies'].items():
            print(f"{name:<30} {info['energy']:<15.2e} {info['precision']:<12}-bit")
        
        print("=" * 70 + "\n")


class ConfigurationWizard:
    """
    Interactive wizard to help users choose optimal configuration.
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def run_wizard() -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """

        """

    @staticmethod
    def _generate_recommendation(
        deployment: str,
        priority: str,
        constraint: str
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Generate configuration recommendation based on inputs."""
        
        # Default configuration
        config = {
            'pattern': 'Mixed-Precision Quantization',
            'precision': '8/4-bit',
            'training_strategy': 'QAT + Knowledge Distillation',
            'compression': '4-8x',
            'speedup': '3-4x',
            'accuracy_loss': '<1%',
            'recommendations': []
        }
        
        # Adjust based on deployment target
        if deployment == '1':  # Cloud GPU
            config['pattern'] = 'Mixed-Precision Quantization'
            config['precision'] = '8/4-bit'
            config['recommendations'].append('Use AMP for training acceleration')
            config['recommendations'].append('Enable TensorRT for inference')
            
        elif deployment == '2':  # Edge Device
            config['pattern'] = 'Ternary Neural Networks'
            config['precision'] = '2-bit (ternary)'
            config['compression'] = '16x'
            config['speedup'] = '8-16x'
            config['accuracy_loss'] = '2-5%'
            config['recommendations'].append('Use progressive quantization')
            config['recommendations'].append('Apply pruning before quantization')
            
        elif deployment == '3':  # IoT
            config['pattern'] = 'Binary Neural Networks'
            config['precision'] = '1-bit (binary)'
            config['compression'] = '32x'
            config['speedup'] = '16-32x'
            config['accuracy_loss'] = '5-10%'
            config['recommendations'].append('Train from scratch with binary weights')
            config['recommendations'].append('Use custom hardware accelerators if available')
            
        elif deployment == '4':  # Server CPU
            config['pattern'] = 'Mixed-Precision Quantization'
            config['precision'] = '8-bit'
            config['recommendations'].append('Use INT8 operations with AVX-512')
            config['recommendations'].append('Enable OpenMP for parallelization')
        
        # Adjust based on priority
        if priority == '1':  # Maximum accuracy
            config['training_strategy'] = 'Progressive Quantization + Knowledge Distillation'
            config['recommendations'].append('Use longer fine-tuning period')
            config['recommendations'].append('Keep first/last layers at higher precision')
            
        elif priority == '3':  # Maximum efficiency
            if deployment != '3':  # Not already binary
                config['pattern'] = 'Ternary Neural Networks'
                config['precision'] = '2-bit'
            config['recommendations'].append('Combine with pruning for maximum compression')
        
        # Adjust based on constraints
        if constraint == '1':  # Latency critical
            config['recommendations'].append('Use batch size = 1 for minimum latency')
            config['recommendations'].append('Enable operator fusion')
            
        elif constraint == '2':  # Memory limited
            config['recommendations'].append('Use gradient checkpointing during training')
            config['recommendations'].append('Export only quantized weights')
            
        elif constraint == '3':  # Energy limited
            if config['pattern'] == 'Mixed-Precision Quantization':
                config['pattern'] = 'Ternary Neural Networks'
                config['precision'] = '2-bit'
            config['recommendations'].append('Optimize for minimal memory access')
            config['recommendations'].append('Use static quantization ranges')
        
        return config

class BenchmarkSuite:
    """
    Comprehensive benchmarking suite for all patterns.
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def run_comprehensive_benchmark(
        input_shape: Tuple[int, ...] = (1, 3, 32, 32),
        num_classes: int = 10,
        num_iterations: int = 100
    ):
        """
        Run comprehensive benchmark across all patterns.
        
        Args:
            input_shape: Input tensor shape
            num_classes: Number of output classes
            num_iterations: Number of iterations for benchmarking
        """
        print("\n" + "=" * 70)
        print("COMPREHENSIVE BENCHMARK SUITE")
        print("=" * 70)
        print(f"\nConfiguration:")
        print(f"  Input Shape: {input_shape}")
        print(f"  Num Classes: {num_classes}")
        print(f"  Iterations: {num_iterations}")
        print("=" * 70 + "\n")
        
        device = 'cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu'
        
        # Define models to benchmark
        models = {
            'FP32 Baseline': SimpleConvNet(num_classes=num_classes),
            'Binary Network': BinaryNet(num_classes=num_classes),
            'Ternary Network': TernaryNet(num_classes=num_classes),
            'Mixed-Precision (8/4)': MixedPrecisionNet(
                num_classes=num_classes,
                precision_config={
                    'conv1': (8, 8), 'conv2': (4, 4),
                    'conv3': (4, 4), 'conv4': (4, 4),
                    'fc1': (4, 4), 'fc2': (8, 8)
                }
            ),
            'Mixed-Precision (8/8)': MixedPrecisionNet(
                num_classes=num_classes,
                precision_config={
                    'conv1': (8, 8), 'conv2': (8, 8),
                    'conv3': (8, 8), 'conv4': (8, 8),
                    'fc1': (8, 8), 'fc2': (8, 8)
                }
            ),
        }
        
        results = {}
        
        for name, model in models.items():
            print(f"Benchmarking: {name}")
            print("-" * 70)
            
            # Inference benchmark
            inference_results = benchmark_inference(
                model, input_shape, num_iterations, device
            )
            
            # Memory analysis
            param_size = sum(p.numel() * p.element_size() for p in model.parameters())
            param_size_mb = param_size / (1024 * 1024)
            
            # Energy estimation
            estimator = EnergyEstimator()
            energy_info = estimator.estimate_model_energy(model, input_shape)
            
            # Compression analysis
            analyzer = ModelCompressionAnalyzer()
            analysis = analyzer.analyze_model(model, name, input_shape)
            
            results[name] = {
                'inference_time_ms': inference_results['avg_inference_time_ms'],
                'throughput_fps': inference_results['throughput_fps'],
                'model_size_mb': param_size_mb,
                'energy_savings': energy_info['energy_savings_percent'],
                'compression_ratio': analysis.get('compression_ratio', 1.0),
                'parameters': analysis['total_parameters']
            }
            
            print()
        
        # Print comparison table
        BenchmarkSuite._print_comparison_table(results)
        
        # Generate plots
        BenchmarkSuite._plot_benchmark_results(results)
        
        return results
    
    @staticmethod
    def _print_comparison_table(results: Dict[str, Dict[str, float]]):
        """Print formatted comparison table."""
        print("\n" + "=" * 100)
        print("BENCHMARK RESULTS COMPARISON")
        print("=" * 100)
        
        print(f"\n{'Model':<25} {'Inf. Time':<12} {'Throughput':<12} {'Size (MB)':<12} "
              f"{'Energy ↓':<12} {'Compress.':<10}")
        print("-" * 100)
        
        # Sort by inference time
        sorted_results = sorted(results.items(), key=lambda x: x[1]['inference_time_ms'])
        
        for name, metrics in sorted_results:
            print(f"{name:<25} "
                  f"{metrics['inference_time_ms']:<12.2f} "
                  f"{metrics['throughput_fps']:<12.2f} "
                  f"{metrics['model_size_mb']:<12.2f} "
                  f"{metrics['energy_savings']:<12.1f}% "
                  f"{metrics['compression_ratio']:<10.2f}x")
        
        print("=" * 100)
        
        # Find best in each category
        best_speed = min(results.items(), key=lambda x: x[1]['inference_time_ms'])
        best_size = min(results.items(), key=lambda x: x[1]['model_size_mb'])
        best_energy = max(results.items(), key=lambda x: x[1]['energy_savings'])
        
        print(f"\nBest Performance:")
        print(f"  Fastest: {best_speed[0]} ({best_speed[1]['inference_time_ms']:.2f}ms)")
        print(f"  Smallest: {best_size[0]} ({best_size[1]['model_size_mb']:.2f}MB)")
        print(f"  Most Efficient: {best_energy[0]} ({best_energy[1]['energy_savings']:.1f}% savings)")
        print("=" * 100 + "\n")

class ImageClassificationPipeline:
    """
    Complete image classification pipeline with energy-efficient inference.
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        model: nn.Module,
        class_names: List[str],
        device: str = 'cuda',
        use_monitoring: bool = True
    ):
        """
        Initialize classification pipeline.
        
        Args:
            model: Trained model
            class_names: List of class names
            device: Device to run on
            use_monitoring: Whether to enable performance monitoring
        """
        self.model = model
        self.class_names = class_names
        self.device = device
        
        self.model.to(device)
        self.model.eval()
        
        if use_monitoring:
            self.monitor = PerformanceMonitor(model.__class__.__name__)
        else:
            self.monitor = None
        
        # Image preprocessing
        self.transform = self._create_transform()
    
    def _create_transform(self):
        """Create image preprocessing transform."""
        try:
            from torchvision import transforms
            return transforms.Compose([
                transforms.Resize((32, 32)),
                transforms.ToTensor(),
                transforms.Normalize(
                    mean=[0.485, 0.456, 0.406],
                    std=[0.229, 0.224, 0.225]
                )
            ])
        except ImportError:
            print("Warning: torchvision not available, using basic transform")
            return None
    
    def predict(
        self,
        image: torch.Tensor,
        top_k: int = 5
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Predict class for a single image.
        
        Args:
            image: Input image tensor
            top_k: Number of top predictions to return
            
        Returns:
            Dictionary with predictions and metadata
        """
        # Ensure correct shape
        if image.dim() == 3:
            image = image.unsqueeze(0)
        
        image = image.to(self.device)
        
        # Inference
        start_time = time.time()
        with torch.no_grad():
            output = self.model(image)
            probabilities = F.softmax(output, dim=1)
        inference_time = time.time() - start_time
        
        # Log performance
        if self.monitor:
            self.monitor.log_inference(inference_time, 1)
        
        # Get top-k predictions
        top_probs, top_indices = probabilities.topk(top_k, dim=1)
        
        predictions = []
        for prob, idx in zip(top_probs[0], top_indices[0]):
            predictions.append({
                'class': self.class_names[idx.item()],
                'class_id': idx.item(),
                'probability': prob.item()
            })
        
        return {
            'predictions': predictions,
            'inference_time_ms': inference_time * 1000,
            'top_prediction': predictions[0]
        }
    
    def predict_batch(
        self,
        images: torch.Tensor
    ) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """
        Predict classes for a batch of images.
        
        Args:
            images: Batch of image tensors
            
        Returns:
            List of prediction dictionaries
        """
        images = images.to(self.device)
        
        start_time = time.time()
        with torch.no_grad():
            outputs = self.model(images)
            probabilities = F.softmax(outputs, dim=1)
        inference_time = time.time() - start_time
        
        if self.monitor:
            self.monitor.log_inference(inference_time, images.size(0))
        
        # Get predictions for each image
        _, predictions = probabilities.max(1)
        
        results = []
        for i, (pred_idx, probs) in enumerate(zip(predictions, probabilities)):
            results.append({
                'class': self.class_names[pred_idx.item()],
                'class_id': pred_idx.item(),
                'probability': probs[pred_idx].item(),
                'all_probabilities': probs.cpu().numpy()
            })
        
        return results
    
    def get_performance_stats(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Get performance statistics."""
        if self.monitor:
            return self.monitor.get_statistics()
        return {}

    """Tutorial: Basic usage of energy efficiency patterns."""
    print("\n" + "=" * 70)
    print("TUTORIAL: Basic Usage")
    print("=" * 70 + "\n")
    
    print("1. Creating a Mixed-Precision Model")

# Define precision for each layer
precision_config = {
    'conv1': (8, 8),   # 8-bit weights and activations
    'conv2': (4, 4),   # 4-bit weights and activations
    'fc1': (4, 4),
    'fc2': (8, 8)      # Higher precision for output layer
}

# Create model

# Train normally with PyTorch

criterion = torch.nn.CrossEntropyLoss()

for epoch in range(num_epochs):
    for inputs, targets in train_loader:
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        outputs = model(inputs)
        loss = criterion(outputs, targets)
        loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()
""")

# This provides 2-3x speedup with minimal accuracy loss!
""")

    student_model=student,

    alpha=0.7
)

# Train with distillation

    train_loader, val_loader, num_epochs=10
)

# Student model now has better accuracy!

        # Simulate varying inference times

def demo_pruning_quantization():
    """Demonstrate combining pruning with quantization."""
    print("\n" + "=" * 70)
    print("PRUNING + QUANTIZATION DEMONSTRATION")
    print("=" * 70 + "\n")
    
    # Create model
    model = MixedPrecisionNet(num_classes=10)
    
    print("Original Model:")
    analyzer = ModelCompressionAnalyzer()
    original_analysis = analyzer.analyze_model(model, "Original")
    print(f"  Parameters: {original_analysis['total_parameters']:,}")
    
    # Apply pruning
    print("\nApplying 50% magnitude pruning...")
    pruner = ModelPruner(model)
    pruner.magnitude_prune(amount=0.5)
    
    # Check sparsity
    pruner.print_sparsity_report()
    
    # Quantization is already applied (MixedPrecisionNet)
    print("Model uses mixed-precision quantization (8/4-bit)")
    
    # Final analysis
    print("\nFinal Model:")
    final_analysis = analyzer.analyze_model(model, "Pruned + Quantized")
    print(f"  Parameters: {final_analysis['total_parameters']:,}")
    print(f"  Compression: {final_analysis['compression_ratio']:.2f}x")
    print(f"  Sparsity: 50%")
    print(f"  Effective Compression: ~{final_analysis['compression_ratio'] * 2:.1f}x")
    
    print("\n" + "=" * 70 + "\n")

validator.validate_numerical_accuracy(baseline, model, test_loader)

# 4. Export
exporter = ModelExporter()
exporter.export_to_torchscript(model, "model.pt")

PERFORMANCE EXPECTATIONS:
=========================

Training Time:
- FP32 Baseline: 1x
- AMP (FP16): 0.4-0.5x (2-2.5x faster)
- Mixed-Precision: 0.5-0.6x (1.7-2x faster)

Inference Time:
- FP32 Baseline: 1x
- Mixed-Precision (8-bit): 0.25-0.33x (3-4x faster)
- Ternary: 0.06-0.12x (8-16x faster)
- Binary: 0.03-0.06x (16-32x faster)

Model Size:
- FP32 Baseline: 1x
- Mixed-Precision (8/4-bit): 0.125-0.25x (4-8x smaller)
- Ternary: 0.06x (16x smaller)
- Binary: 0.03x (32x smaller)

Accuracy Impact:
- AMP: <0.1% loss
- Mixed-Precision (8-bit): <1% loss
- Ternary: 2-5% loss
- Binary: 5-10% loss

HARDWARE-SPECIFIC NOTES:
========================

NVIDIA GPU:
- Best for: Mixed-Precision (8-bit), AMP
- Use: TensorRT, CUDA, cuDNN
- Speedup: 3-4x with INT8

Intel CPU:
- Best for: Mixed-Precision (8-bit)
- Use: OpenVINO, AVX-512, VNNI
- Speedup: 2-3x with INT8

ARM Mobile:
- Best for: Ternary Networks
- Use: NNAPI, XNNPACK
- Speedup: 8-16x

ARM Cortex-M:
- Best for: Binary Networks
- Use: CMSIS-NN
- Speedup: 16-32x

Edge TPU:
- Best for: 8-bit quantization
- Use: TensorFlow Lite
- Speedup: 10-20x

TROUBLESHOOTING:
================

Issue: Accuracy drops significantly
Solutions:
1. Use progressive quantization instead of direct
2. Apply knowledge distillation
3. Increase precision for sensitive layers
4. Use per-channel quantization
5. Calibrate on more representative data

Issue: Slow inference despite quantization
Solutions:
1. Enable hardware-specific optimizations
2. Check if quantized ops are actually used
3. Reduce batch size for lower latency
4. Apply operator fusion
5. Profile to find bottlenecks

Issue: Memory issues during training
Solutions:
1. Use gradient checkpointing
2. Reduce batch size
3. Enable AMP to reduce memory
4. Use gradient accumulation
5. Clear cache regularly

Issue: Model export fails
Solutions:
1. Ensure all ops are supported
2. Use torch.jit.trace instead of script
3. Simplify model architecture
4. Update PyTorch/ONNX versions
5. Check for dynamic shapes

BEST PRACTICES:
===============

1. Always validate on representative data
2. Start with higher precision and reduce gradually
3. Keep first and last layers at higher precision
4. Use knowledge distillation for better accuracy
5. Calibrate quantization on validation set
6. Monitor performance in production
7. Version control model configurations
8. Document all hyperparameters
9. Test on target hardware before deployment
10. Set up proper monitoring and alerting

class PerformanceOptimizationGuide:
    """
    Detailed guide for optimizing performance.
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def print_optimization_guide():
        """
        Print comprehensive optimization guide.
        """
        guide = """
╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║              PERFORMANCE OPTIMIZATION GUIDE                          ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

1. TRAINING OPTIMIZATION
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

A. Use Automatic Mixed Precision (AMP)
   ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │ trainer = LowPrecisionTrainer(model, use_amp=True)             │
   │ # Provides 2-3x speedup with minimal code changes              │
   └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
   
   Benefits:
   • 2-3x faster training
   • 50% memory reduction
   • Minimal accuracy impact (<0.1%)
   
   Best Practices:
   • Use on NVIDIA GPUs with Tensor Cores (V100, A100, RTX 30xx)
   • Start with loss scaling factor of 65536
   • Monitor for gradient underflow/overflow
   • Keep batch normalization in FP32

B. Gradient Accumulation
   ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │ accumulation_steps = 4                                         │
   │ for i, (inputs, targets) in enumerate(train_loader):          │
   │     loss = model(inputs, targets) / accumulation_steps        │
   │     loss.backward()                                            │
   │     if (i + 1) % accumulation_steps == 0:                     │
   │         optimizer.step()                                       │
   │         optimizer.zero_grad()                                  │
   └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
   
   Use When:
   • GPU memory is limited
   • Want larger effective batch size
   • Training large models

C. DataLoader Optimization
   ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │ loader = DataLoader(                                           │
   │     dataset,                                                   │
   │     batch_size=32,                                            │
   │     num_workers=4,        # Use multiple workers              │
   │     pin_memory=True,      # Faster GPU transfer               │
   │     persistent_workers=True  # Keep workers alive             │
   │ )                                                              │
   └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

2. QUANTIZATION OPTIMIZATION
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

A. Choose Right Precision per Layer
   ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │ Layer Type          Recommended Precision                      │
   │ ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────│
   │ First Conv          8-bit (sensitive to input)                │
   │ Middle Convs        4-bit (less sensitive)                    │
   │ Classifier          8-bit (critical for accuracy)             │
   │ Batch Norm          FP32 (always keep full precision)         │
   │ Activation          Same as weights or higher                 │
   └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

B. Calibration Best Practices
   • Use 500-1000 representative samples
   • Include diverse examples from each class
   • Calibrate on validation set, not training set
   • Re-calibrate if input distribution changes

C. Quantization-Aware Training (QAT)
   ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │ # Fine-tune for 5-10 epochs with quantization                 │
   │ qat_trainer = QuantizationAwareTraining(model, target_bits)   │
   │ qat_trainer.prepare_qat()                                     │
   │ qat_trainer.train_qat(train_loader, optimizer, criterion)     │
   └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
   
   When to Use:
   • Accuracy drops >2% with post-training quantization
   • Deploying to production
   • Have time for additional training

   │   batch_size = 32-128  # Maximum throughput                   │
