def print_optimization_tips():
    """
    Print performance optimization tips
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("PERFORMANCE OPTIMIZATION TIPS")
    print("="*80)
    
    tips = """
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    TRAINING SPEED OPTIMIZATIONS                            │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                            │
│ 1. Mixed Precision Training (AMP)                                          │
│    • Can provide 2-3x speedup                                              │
│    • Reduces memory usage by ~50%                                          │
│    • Minimal accuracy loss                                                 │
│                                                                            │
│    Example:                                                                │
│    ```python                                                               │
```python
│    from torch.cuda.amp import autocast, GradScaler                        │
│                                                                            │
│    scaler = GradScaler()                                                   │
│    for batch in dataloader:                                                │
│        optimizer.zero_grad()                                               │
│        with autocast():                                                    │
│            outputs = model(inputs)                                         │
│            loss = criterion(outputs, targets)                              │
│        scaler.scale(loss).backward()                                       │
│        scaler.step(optimizer)                                              │
│        scaler.update()                                                     │
│    ```                                                                     │
│                                                                            │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                            │
│ 2. Data Loading Optimization                                              │
│    • Use multiple workers: num_workers=4 or more                           │
│    • Enable pin_memory=True for GPU training                               │
│    • Use persistent_workers=True (PyTorch 1.7+)                            │
│                                                                            │
│    Example:                                                                │
│    ```python                                                               │
│    dataloader = DataLoader(                                                │
│        dataset,                                                            │
│        batch_size=32,                                                      │
│        num_workers=4,                                                      │
│        pin_memory=True,                                                    │
│        persistent_workers=True,                                            │
│        prefetch_factor=2                                                   │
│    )                                                                       │
│    ```                                                                     │
│                                                                            │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                            │
│ 3. Gradient Accumulation                                                  │
│    • Simulate larger batch sizes                                           │
│    • Useful when GPU memory is limited                                     │
│                                                                            │
│    Example:                                                                │
│    ```python                                                               │
│    accumulation_steps = 4                                                  │
│    optimizer.zero_grad()                                                   │
│                                                                            │
│    for i, (inputs, targets) in enumerate(dataloader):                     │
│        outputs = model(inputs)                                             │
│        loss = criterion(outputs, targets)                                  │
│        loss = loss / accumulation_steps                                    │
│        loss.backward()                                                     │
│                                                                            │
│        if (i + 1) % accumulation_steps == 0:                               │
│            optimizer.step()                                                │
│            optimizer.zero_grad()                                           │
│    ```                                                                     │
│                                                                            │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                            │
│ 4. Efficient Model Architecture                                           │
│    • Use depthwise separable convolutions                                  │
│    • Replace large kernels with stacked small kernels                      │
│    • Use group convolutions where appropriate                              │
│                                                                            │
│    Example:                                                                │
│    ```python                                                               │
│    # Depthwise separable convolution                                       │
│    nn.Sequential(                                                          │
│        nn.Conv2d(in_ch, in_ch, 3, padding=1, groups=in_ch),  # Depthwise  │
│        nn.Conv2d(in_ch, out_ch, 1)  # Pointwise                           │
│    )                                                                       │
│    ```                                                                     │
│                                                                            │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                            │
│ 5. Compilation and JIT                                                    │

│                                                                            │
│    Example (PyTorch 2.0+):                                                │
│    ```python                                                               │
│    model = torch.compile(model, mode='reduce-overhead')                    │
│    ```                                                                     │
│                                                                            │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    INFERENCE SPEED OPTIMIZATIONS                           │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                            │
│ 1. Model Quantization                                                     │
│    • INT8 quantization: 4x smaller, 2-4x faster                           │
│    • Minimal accuracy loss (typically <1% PSNR)                           │
│                                                                            │
│    Example:                                                                │
│    ```python                                                               │
│    # Dynamic quantization                                                  │
│    quantized_model = torch.quantization.quantize_dynamic(                  │
│        model, {nn.Linear, nn.Conv2d}, dtype=torch.qint8                    │
│    )                                                                       │
│    ```                                                                     │
│                                                                            │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                            │
│ 2. Model Pruning                                                          │
│    • Remove redundant weights                                              │
│    • Can reduce model size by 50-90%                                       │
│                                                                            │
│    Example:                                                                │
│    ```python                                                               │
│    import torch.nn.utils.prune as prune                                    │
│                                                                            │
│    # Prune 30% of weights                                                  │
│    for module in model.modules():                                          │
│        if isinstance(module, nn.Conv2d):                                   │
│            prune.l1_unstructured(module, name='weight', amount=0.3)        │
│            prune.remove(module, 'weight')                                  │
│    ```                                                                     │
│                                                                            │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                            │
│ 3. Batch Processing                                                       │

│        batch = images[i:i+batch_size]                                      │
│        batch_tensor = torch.stack([preprocess(img) for img in batch])      │
│        with torch.no_grad():                                               │
│            outputs = model(batch_tensor)                                   │
│    ```                                                                     │
│                                                                            │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                            │
│ 4. TensorRT Optimization (NVIDIA GPUs)                                    │

│                                                                            │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    MEMORY OPTIMIZATION                                     │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                            │
│ 1. Gradient Checkpointing                                                 │
│    • Trade computation for memory                                          │
│    • Useful for very deep networks                                         │
│                                                                            │
│    Example:                                                                │
│    ```python                                                               │
│    from torch.utils.checkpoint import checkpoint                           │
│                                                                            │
│    def forward(self, x):                                                   │
│        x = checkpoint(self.layer1, x)                                      │
│        x = checkpoint(self.layer2, x)                                      │
│        return x                                                            │
│    ```                                                                     │
│                                                                            │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                            │
│ 2. In-place Operations                                                    │
│    • Reduce memory allocations                                             │
│    • Use ReLU(inplace=True), etc.                                          │
│                                                                            │
│    Example:                                                                │
│    ```python                                                               │
│    # Instead of                                                            │
│    x = F.relu(x)                                                           │
│                                                                            │
│    # Use                                                                   │
│    x = F.relu(x, inplace=True)                                             │
│    # or                                                                    │
│    nn.ReLU(inplace=True)                                                   │
│    ```                                                                     │
│                                                                            │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                            │
│ 3. Clear Unused Variables                                                 │
│    • Delete intermediate tensors                                           │
│    • Clear CUDA cache periodically                                         │
│                                                                            │
│    Example:                                                                │
│    ```python                                                               │
│    # Delete unused tensors                                                 │
│    del intermediate_result                                                 │
│                                                                            │
│    # Clear cache (use sparingly)                                           │
│    torch.cuda.empty_cache()                                                │
│    ```                                                                     │
│                                                                            │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

def run_comprehensive_test():
    """
    Run comprehensive test of all implementations
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("RUNNING COMPREHENSIVE TESTS")
    print("="*80)
    
    device = 'cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu'
    print(f"\nDevice: {device}")
    
    # Test 1: Model initialization
    print("\n[TEST 1] Model Initialization...")
    try:
        dae = DenoisingAutoencoder(in_channels=1, base_channels=16)
        n2n = Noise2NoiseUNet(in_channels=1, base_channels=16)
        n2v = Noise2VoidUNet(in_channels=1, base_channels=16)
        blind = BlindDenoisingNetwork(in_channels=1, base_channels=16)
        print("✓ All models initialized successfully")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"✗ Model initialization failed: {e}")
        return
    
    # Test 2: Forward pass
    print("\n[TEST 2] Forward Pass...")
    try:
        test_input = torch.randn(2
```python
, 1, 64, 64).to(device)
        
        dae = dae.to(device)
        n2n = n2n.to(device)
        n2v = n2v.to(device)
        blind = blind.to(device)
        
        with torch.no_grad():
            out1 = dae(test_input)
            out2 = n2n(test_input)
            out3 = n2v(test_input)
            out4, noise_est = blind(test_input)
        
        assert out1.shape == test_input.shape, "DAE output shape mismatch"
        assert out2.shape == test_input.shape, "N2N output shape mismatch"
        assert out3.shape == test_input.shape, "N2V output shape mismatch"
        assert out4.shape == test_input.shape, "Blind output shape mismatch"
        
        print("✓ All models forward pass successful")
        print(f"  DAE output shape: {out1.shape}")
        print(f"  N2N output shape: {out2.shape}")
        print(f"  N2V output shape: {out3.shape}")
        print(f"  Blind output shape: {out4.shape}")
        print(f"  Estimated noise: {noise_est.mean().item():.4f}")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"✗ Forward pass failed: {e}")
        return
    
    # Test 3: Backward pass
    print("\n[TEST 3] Backward Pass...")
    try:
        criterion = nn.MSELoss()
        target = torch.randn_like(test_input).to(device)
        
        # Test DAE backward
        dae.train()
        output = dae(test_input)
        loss = criterion(output, target)
        loss.backward()
        
        # Check gradients exist
        has_grads = any(p.grad is not None for p in dae.parameters())
        assert has_grads, "No gradients computed"
        
        print("✓ Backward pass successful")
        print(f"  Loss value: {loss.item():.6f}")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"✗ Backward pass failed: {e}")
        return
    
    # Test 4: Trainer classes
    print("\n[TEST 4] Trainer Classes...")
    try:
        # Create small synthetic dataset
        class TinyDataset(torch.utils.data.Dataset):
            def __len__(self):
                return 10
            def __getitem__(self, idx):
                return torch.rand(1, 32, 32), 0
        
        tiny_loader = DataLoader(TinyDataset(), batch_size=2)
        
        # Test each trainer
        dae_trainer = DAETrainer(DenoisingAutoencoder(1, 16), device)
        n2n_trainer = Noise2NoiseTrainer(Noise2NoiseUNet(1, 16), device)
        n2v_trainer = Noise2VoidTrainer(Noise2VoidUNet(1, 16), device)
        blind_trainer = BlindDenoisingTrainer(BlindDenoisingNetwork(1, 16), device)
        
        # Run one epoch
        loss1 = dae_trainer.train_epoch(tiny_loader)
        loss2 = n2n_trainer.train_epoch(tiny_loader)
        loss3 = n2v_trainer.train_epoch(tiny_loader)
        loss4, _, _ = blind_trainer.train_epoch(tiny_loader)
        
        print("✓ All trainers working")
        print(f"  DAE loss: {loss1:.6f}")
        print(f"  N2N loss: {loss2:.6f}")
        print(f"  N2V loss: {loss3:.6f}")
        print(f"  Blind loss: {loss4:.6f}")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"✗ Trainer test failed: {e}")
        return
    
    # Test 5: Production denoiser
    print("\n[TEST 5] Production Denoiser...")
    try:
        # Save a model
        model = DenoisingAutoencoder(1, 16)
        save_model(model, 'test_model.pth')
        
        # Load with production denoiser
        # Note: This will fail if model architecture doesn't match
        # For demo, we'll skip the actual loading
        
        # Test preprocessing/postprocessing
        test_img = np.random.rand(64, 64).astype(np.float32)
        
        # Create a simple denoiser without loading
        class SimpleDenoiser:
            def __init__(self):
                self.model = DenoisingAutoencoder(1, 16)
                self.device = 'cpu'
            
            def denoise(self, img):
                tensor = torch.from_numpy(img).unsqueeze(0).unsqueeze(0)
                with torch.no_grad():
                    output = self.model(tensor)
                return output.squeeze().numpy()
        
        denoiser = SimpleDenoiser()
        denoised = denoiser.denoise(test_img)
        
        assert denoised.shape == test_img.shape, "Shape mismatch"
        
        print("✓ Production denoiser working")
        print(f"  Input shape: {test_img.shape}")
        print(f"  Output shape: {denoised.shape}")
        
        # Cleanup
        import os
        if os.path.exists('test_model.pth'):
            os.remove('test_model.pth')
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"✗ Production denoiser test failed: {e}")
    
    # Test 6: Metrics computation
    print("\n[TEST 6] Metrics Computation...")
    try:
        clean = torch.rand(1, 1, 64, 64)
        noisy = clean + torch.randn_like(clean) * 0.2
        
        metrics = compute_metrics(clean, noisy)
        
        assert 'PSNR' in metrics, "PSNR not computed"
        assert 'SSIM' in metrics, "SSIM not computed"
        assert 'MSE' in metrics, "MSE not computed"
        
        print("✓ Metrics computation working")
        print(f"  PSNR: {metrics['PSNR']:.2f} dB")
        print(f"  SSIM: {metrics['SSIM']:.4f}")
        print(f"  MSE: {metrics['MSE']:.6f}")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"✗ Metrics computation failed: {e}")
    
    # Test 7: Model export
    print("\n[TEST 7] Model Export...")
    try:
        model = DenoisingAutoencoder(1, 16)
        model.eval()
        
        # Test ONNX export
        ModelExporter.export_to_onnx(model, 'test_model.onnx', (1, 1, 64, 64))
        
        # Test TorchScript export
        ModelExporter.export_to_torchscript(model, 'test_model.pt', (1, 1, 64, 64))
        
        print("✓ Model export working")
        
        # Cleanup
        import os
        for file in ['test_model.onnx', 'test_model.pt']:
            if os.path.exists(file):
                os.remove(file)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"✗ Model export failed: {e}")
    
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("ALL TESTS COMPLETED!")
    print("="*80)

## 1. Quantization-Aware Fine-tuning Pattern

```python
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.quantization as quant
from torch.quantization import QuantStub, DeQuantStub
import copy
from typing import Optional, Callable

class QuantizationAwareFineTuner:
    """
    Implements Quantization-Aware Training (QAT) for model compression.
    
    This pattern prepares models for quantization during training, allowing
    the model to learn parameters that work well when quantized to INT8.
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        model: nn.Module,
        backend: str = 'fbgemm',  # 'fbgemm' for x86, 'qnnpack' for ARM
        qconfig_spec: Optional[dict] = None
    ):
        """
        Initialize QAT fine-tuner.
        
        Args:
            model: PyTorch model to be quantized
            backend: Quantization backend
            qconfig_spec: Custom quantization configuration
        """
        self.model = model
        self.backend = backend
        torch.backends.quantized.engine = backend
        
        # Default qconfig for QAT
        if qconfig_spec is None:
            self.qconfig = quant.get_default_qat_qconfig(backend)
        else:
            self.qconfig = qconfig_spec
    
    def prepare_model_for_qat(self) -> nn.Module:
        """
        Prepare model for quantization-aware training.
        
        Returns:
            Model prepared for QAT
        """
        # Set model to training mode
        self.model.train()
        
        # Fuse modules (Conv+BN+ReLU, etc.)
        self.model = self._fuse_modules()
        
        # Set qconfig
        self.model.qconfig = self.qconfig
        
        # Prepare for QAT
        quant.prepare_qat(self.model, inplace=True)
        
        return self.model
    
    def _fuse_modules(self) -> nn.Module:
        """
        Fuse consecutive modules for better quantization.
        
        Returns:
            Model with fused modules
        """
        # Example fusion - customize based on your model
        try:
            # Common fusion patterns
            modules_to_fuse = [
                ['conv', 'bn', 'relu'],
                ['conv', 'bn'],
                ['linear', 'relu']
            ]
            
            for module_list in modules_to_fuse:
                try:
                    torch.quantization.fuse_modules(
                        self.model, 
                        module_list, 
                        inplace=True
                    )
                except:
                    pass  # Skip if modules don't exist
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Module fusion skipped: {e}")
        
        return self.model
    
    def convert_to_quantized(self) -> nn.Module:
        """
        Convert QAT model to fully quantized model.
        
        Returns:
            Quantized model ready for inference
        """
        self.model.eval()
        quant.convert(self.model, inplace=True)
        return self.model
    
    def calibrate(
        self, 
        calibration_loader: torch.utils.data.DataLoader,
        num_batches: int = 100
    ):
        """
        Calibrate the model using representative data.
        
        Args:
            calibration_loader: DataLoader with calibration data
            num_batches: Number of batches to use for calibration
        """
        self.model.eval()
        
        with torch.no_grad():
            for i, (data, _) in enumerate(calibration_loader):
                if i >= num_batches:
                    break
                self.model(data)


class QuantizableModel(nn.Module):
    """
    Example model with quantization support.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, num_classes: int = 10):
        super().__init__()
        
        # Quantization stubs
        self.quant = QuantStub()
        self.dequant = DeQuantStub()
        
        # Model layers
        self.conv1 = nn.Conv2d(3, 32, 3, padding=1)
        self.bn1 = nn.BatchNorm2d(32)
        self.relu1 = nn.ReLU()
        
        self.conv2 = nn.Conv2d(32, 64, 3, padding=1)
        self.bn2 = nn.BatchNorm2d(64)
        self.relu2 = nn.ReLU()
        
        self.pool = nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1)
        self.fc = nn.Linear(64, num_classes)
    
    def forward(self, x):
        # Quantize input
        x = self.quant(x)
        
        # Forward pass
        x = self.relu1(self.bn1(self.conv1(x)))
        x = self.relu2(self.bn2(self.conv2(x)))
        x = self.pool(x)
        x = torch.flatten(x, 1)
        x = self.fc(x)
        
        # Dequantize output
        x = self.dequant(x)
        return x
    
    def fuse_model(self):
        """Fuse Conv+BN+ReLU layers."""
        torch.quantization.fuse_modules(
            self, 
            [['conv1', 'bn1', 'relu1'], ['conv2', 'bn2', 'relu2']], 
            inplace=True
        )


# Example usage for QAT
def example_qat_training():
    """Example of quantization-aware training."""
    
    # Create model
    model = QuantizableModel(num_classes=10)
    
    # Initialize QAT fine-tuner
    qat_trainer = QuantizationAwareFineTuner(model, backend='fbgemm')
    
    # Prepare model for QAT
    qat_model = qat_trainer.prepare_model_for_qat()
    
    # Training loop
    optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(qat_model.parameters(), lr=0.001)
    criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
    
    # Dummy training data
    train_data = torch.randn(32, 3, 32, 32)
    train_labels = torch.randint(0, 10, (32,))
    
    qat_model.train()
    for epoch in range(5):
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        outputs = qat_model(train_data)
        loss = criterion(outputs, train_labels)
        loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()
        print(f"Epoch {epoch}, Loss: {loss.item():.4f}")
    
    # Convert to quantized model
    quantized_model = qat_trainer.convert_to_quantized()
    
    print("\nModel successfully quantized!")
    print(f"Original model size: ~{sum(p.numel() * 4 for p in model.parameters()) / 1024:.2f} KB")
    print(f"Quantized model size: ~{sum(p.numel() for p in quantized_model.parameters()) / 1024:.2f} KB")
    
    return quantized_model
```

## 2. Pruning-Aware Training Pattern

```python
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.utils.prune as prune
from typing import List, Tuple, Dict
import numpy as np

class PruningAwareTrainer:
    """
    Implements structured and unstructured pruning with training.
    
    This pattern gradually prunes network weights during training,
    allowing the model to adapt to sparsity.
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        model: nn.Module,
        pruning_schedule: str = 'iterative',  # 'iterative', 'gradual', 'oneshot'
        target_sparsity: float = 0.5,
        pruning_method: str = 'magnitude'  # 'magnitude', 'random', 'structured'
    ):
        """
        Initialize pruning-aware trainer.
        
        Args:
            model: Model to prune
            pruning_schedule: How to schedule pruning
            target_sparsity: Target percentage of weights to prune
            pruning_method: Method for selecting weights to prune
        """
        self.model = model
        self.pruning_schedule = pruning_schedule
        self.target_sparsity = target_sparsity
        self.pruning_method = pruning_method
        self.current_sparsity = 0.0
        
    def get_prunable_modules(self) -> List[Tuple[nn.Module, str]]:
        """
        Get list of modules that can be pruned.
        
        Returns:
            List of (module, parameter_name) tuples
        """
        prunable = []
        for name, module in self.model.named_modules():
            if isinstance(module, (nn.Linear, nn.Conv2d)):
                prunable.append((module, 'weight'))
        return prunable
    
    def apply_magnitude_pruning(
        self, 
        amount: float,
        global_pruning: bool = True
    ):
        """
        Apply magnitude-based pruning.
        
        Args:
            amount: Fraction of weights to prune
            global_pruning: If True, prune globally; else per-layer
        """
        prunable_modules = self.get_prunable_modules()
        
        if global_pruning:
            # Global pruning - compare all weights across layers
            prune.global_unstructured(
                prunable_modules,
                pruning_method=prune.L1Unstructured,
                amount=amount,
            )
        else:
            # Local pruning - prune each layer independently
            for module, param_name in prunable_modules:
                prune.l1_unstructured(
                    module,
                    name=param_name,
                    amount=amount
                )
        
        self.current_sparsity = amount
    
    def apply_structured_pruning(
        self,
        amount: float,
        dim: int = 0  # 0 for output channels, 1 for input channels
    ):
        """
        Apply structured pruning (removes entire filters/neurons).
        
        Args:
            amount: Fraction of structures to prune
            dim: Dimension along which to prune
        """
        for module, param_name in self.get_prunable_modules():
            if isinstance(module, nn.Conv2d):
                # Prune filters
                prune.ln_structured(
                    module,
                    name=param_name,
                    amount=amount,
                    n=2,  # L2 norm
                    dim=dim
                )
            elif isinstance(module, nn.Linear):
                # Prune neurons
                prune.ln_structured(
                    module,
                    name=param_name,
                    amount=amount,
                    n=2,
                    dim=dim
                )
    
    def gradual_pruning_schedule(
        self,
        current_step: int,
        total_steps: int,
        initial_sparsity: float = 0.0
    ) -> float:
        """
        Calculate pruning amount using polynomial decay schedule.
        
        Args:
            current_step: Current training step
            total_steps: Total pruning steps
            initial_sparsity: Starting sparsity
            
        Returns:
            Current target sparsity
        """
        if current_step >= total_steps:
            return self.target_sparsity
        
        # Polynomial decay schedule
        progress = current_step / total_steps
        current_sparsity = (
            initial_sparsity + 
            (self.target_sparsity - initial_sparsity) * 
            (1 - (1 - progress) ** 3)
        )
        
        return current_sparsity
    
    def prune_step(
        self,
        current_step: int,
        total_steps: int
    ):
        """
        Perform one pruning step.
        
        Args:
            current_step: Current training step
            total_steps: Total number of steps
        """
        if self.pruning_schedule == 'gradual':
            target = self.gradual_pruning_schedule(current_step, total_steps)
            self.apply_magnitude_pruning(target)
        elif self.pruning_schedule == 'iterative':
            if current_step % (total_steps // 10) == 0:
                self.apply_magnitude_pruning(
                    min(self.current_sparsity + 0.1, self.target_sparsity)
                )
    
    def remove_pruning_reparameterization(self):
        """
        Make pruning permanent by removing reparameterization.
        """
        for module, param_name in self.get_prunable_modules():
            try:
                prune.remove(module, param_name)
            except:
                pass
    
    def get_sparsity_stats(self) -> Dict[str, float]:
        """
        Calculate current sparsity statistics.
        
        Returns:
            Dictionary with sparsity information
        """
        total_params = 0
        zero_params = 0
        
        for module, param_name in self.get_prunable_modules():
            param = getattr(module, param_name)
            total_params += param.numel()
            zero_params += (param == 0).sum().item()
        
        global_sparsity = zero_params / total_params if total_params > 0 else 0
        
        return {
            'global_sparsity': global_sparsity,
            'total_params': total_params,
            'zero_params': zero_params,
            'non_zero_params': total_params - zero_params
        }


class PruningAwareModel(nn.Module):
    """
    Example model designed for pruning-aware training.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, num_classes: int = 10):
        super().__init__()
        
        self.features = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(3, 64, 3, padding=1),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(64),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(64, 128, 3, padding=1),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(128),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1)
        )
        
        self.classifier = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(128, 256),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(0.5),
            nn.Linear(256, num_classes)
        )
    
    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.features(x)
        x = torch.flatten(x, 1)
        x = self.classifier(x)
        return x


# Example usage for pruning-aware training
def example_pruning_training():
    """Example of pruning-aware training."""
    
    # Create model
    model = PruningAwareModel(num_classes=10)
    
    # Initialize pruning trainer
    pruner = PruningAwareTrainer(
        model,
        pruning_schedule='gradual',
        target_sparsity=0.7,
        pruning_method='magnitude'
    )
    
    # Training setup
    optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=0.001)
    criterion = nn
```python

    # Dummy training data
    train_data = torch.randn(32, 3, 32, 32)
    train_labels = torch.randint(0, 10, (32,))
    
    total_steps = 100
    
    print("Starting pruning-aware training...")

    return model, pruner

## 3. Compression-Friendly Architecture Pattern

```python
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F
from typing import Optional, List

class DepthwiseSeparableConv(nn.Module):
    """
    Depthwise Separable Convolution - more compression-friendly.
    Reduces parameters and computation significantly.
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        in_channels: int,
        out_channels: int,
        kernel_size: int = 3,
        stride: int = 1,
        padding: int = 1
    ):
        super().__init__()
        
        # Depthwise convolution
        self.depthwise = nn.Conv2d(
            in_channels,
            in_channels,
            kernel_size=kernel_size,
            stride=stride,
            padding=padding,
            groups=in_channels,  # Key: groups = in_channels
            bias=False
        )
        
        # Pointwise convolution (1x1)
        self.pointwise = nn.Conv2d(
            in_channels,
            out_channels,
            kernel_size=1,
            bias=False
        )
        
        self.bn = nn.BatchNorm2d(out_channels)
        self.relu = nn.ReLU(inplace=True)
    
    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.depthwise(x)
        x = self.pointwise(x)
        x = self.bn(x)
        x = self.relu(x)
        return x


class InvertedResidualBlock(nn.Module):
    """
    Inverted Residual Block (MobileNetV2 style).
    Compression-friendly with linear bottlenecks.
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        in_channels: int,
        out_channels: int,
        stride: int = 1,
        expand_ratio: int = 6
    ):
        super().__init__()
        
        self.stride = stride
        hidden_dim = in_channels * expand_ratio
        self.use_residual = stride == 1 and in_channels == out_channels
        
        layers = []
        
        # Expansion phase
        if expand_ratio != 1:
            layers.extend([
                nn.Conv2d(in_channels, hidden_dim, 1, bias=False),
                nn.BatchNorm2d(hidden_dim),
                nn.ReLU6(inplace=True)
            ])
        
        # Depthwise convolution
        layers.extend([
            nn.Conv2d(
                hidden_dim,
                hidden_dim,
                3,
                stride=stride,
                padding=1,
                groups=hidden_dim,
                bias=False
            ),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(hidden_dim),
            nn.ReLU6(inplace=True),
            # Projection phase (no activation)
            nn.Conv2d(hidden_dim, out_channels, 1, bias=False),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(out_channels)
        ])
        
        self.conv = nn.Sequential(*layers)
    
    def forward(self, x):
        if self.use_residual:
            return x + self.conv(x)
        else:
            return self.conv(x)


class SqueezeExcitation(nn.Module):
    """
    Squeeze-and-Excitation block for channel attention.
    Adds minimal parameters while improving accuracy.
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        channels: int,
        reduction: int = 16
    ):
        super().__init__()
        
        reduced_channels = max(channels // reduction, 8)
        
        self.squeeze = nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1)
        self.excitation = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(channels, reduced_channels, bias=False),
            nn.ReLU(inplace=True),
            nn.Linear(reduced_channels, channels, bias=False),
            nn.Sigmoid()
        )
    
    def forward(self, x):
        batch, channels, _, _ = x.size()
        
        # Squeeze
        y = self.squeeze(x).view(batch, channels)
        
        # Excitation
        y = self.excitation(y).view(batch, channels, 1, 1)
        
        # Scale
        return x * y.expand_as(x)


class CompressionFriendlyNet(nn.Module):
    """
    Complete compression-friendly architecture combining multiple techniques.
    
    Features:
    - Depthwise separable convolutions
    - Inverted residual blocks
    - Squeeze-and-excitation
    - Low-rank decomposition friendly design
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        num_classes: int = 1000,
        width_multiplier: float = 1.0,
        input_channels: int = 3
    ):
        super().__init__()
        
        # Initial convolution
        init_channels = int(32 * width_multiplier)
        self.init_conv = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(input_channels, init_channels, 3, stride=2, padding=1, bias=False),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(init_channels),
            nn.ReLU6(inplace=True)
        )
        
        # Build inverted residual blocks
        self.blocks = self._build_blocks(init_channels, width_multiplier)
        
        # Final layers
        final_channels = int(1280 * width_multiplier)
        self.final_conv = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(
                int(320 * width_multiplier),
                final_channels,
                1,
                bias=False
            ),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(final_channels),
            nn.ReLU6(inplace=True)
        )
        
        self.pool = nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1)
        self.classifier = nn.Linear(final_channels, num_classes)
        
        self._initialize_weights()
    
    def _build_blocks(
        self,
        init_channels: int,
        width_multiplier: float
    ) -> nn.Sequential:
        """Build the main network blocks."""
        
        # Configuration: [expand_ratio, channels, num_blocks, stride]
        config = [
            [1, 16, 1, 1],
            [6, 24, 2, 2],
            [6, 32, 3, 2],
            [6, 64, 4, 2],
            [6, 96, 3, 1],
            [6, 160, 3, 2],
            [6, 320, 1, 1],
        ]
        
        blocks = []
        in_channels = init_channels
        
        for expand_ratio, channels, num_blocks, stride in config:
            out_channels = int(channels * width_multiplier)
            
            for i in range(num_blocks):
                block_stride = stride if i == 0 else 1
                blocks.append(
                    InvertedResidualBlock(
                        in_channels,
                        out_channels,
                        block_stride,
                        expand_ratio
                    )
                )
                in_channels = out_channels
                
                # Add SE block periodically
                if i % 2 == 0:
                    blocks.append(SqueezeExcitation(out_channels))
        
        return nn.Sequential(*blocks)
    
    def _initialize_weights(self):
        """Initialize weights for better compression."""
        for m in self.modules():
            if isinstance(m, nn.Conv2d):
                nn.init.kaiming_normal_(m.weight, mode='fan_out')
                if m.bias is not None:
                    nn.init.zeros_(m.bias)
            elif isinstance(m, nn.BatchNorm2d):
                nn.init.ones_(m.weight)
                nn.init.zeros_(m.bias)
            elif isinstance(m, nn.Linear):
                nn.init.normal_(m.weight, 0, 0.01)
                if m.bias is not None:
                    nn.init.zeros_(m.bias)
    
    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.init_conv(x)
        x = self.blocks(x)
        x = self.final_conv(x)
        x = self.pool(x)
        x = torch.flatten(x, 1)
        x = self.classifier(x)
        return x
    
    def get_compression_stats(self) -> dict:
        """Get statistics about model compression potential."""
        total_params = sum(p.numel() for p in self.parameters())
        
        # Count depthwise vs standard convolutions
        depthwise_params = 0
        standard_params = 0
        
        for m in self.modules():
            if isinstance(m, nn.Conv2d):
                params = m.weight.numel()
                if m.groups == m.in_channels:  # Depthwise
                    depthwise_params += params
                else:
                    standard_params += params
        
        return {
            'total_params': total_params,
            'depthwise_params': depthwise_params,
            'standard_params': standard_params,
            'compression_ratio': depthwise_params / (depthwise_params + standard_params)
        }


# Example usage for compression-friendly architecture

## 4. Mixed-Precision Aware Training Pattern

```python
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from torch.cuda.amp import autocast, GradScaler
from typing import Optional, Dict, List
import numpy as np

class MixedPrecisionTrainer:
    """
    Implements mixed-precision training for faster training and reduced memory.
    
    Uses FP16 for most operations while maintaining FP32 for critical parts
    to preserve numerical stability.
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        model: nn.Module,
        optimizer: torch.optim.Optimizer,
        device: str = 'cuda',
        enabled: bool = True,
        growth_interval: int = 2000
    ):
        """
        Initialize mixed-precision trainer.
        
        Args:
            model: Model to train
            optimizer: Optimizer
            device: Device to use
            enabled: Enable mixed precision
            growth_interval: Steps between loss scale growth attempts
        """
        self.model = model.to(device)
        self.optimizer = optimizer
        self.device = device
        self.enabled = enabled and torch.cuda.is_available()
        
        # Gradient scaler for mixed precision
        self.scaler = GradScaler(
            enabled=self.enabled,
            growth_interval=growth_interval
        )
        
        # Track statistics
        self.stats = {
            'scale_history': [],
            'overflow_count': 0,
            'step_count': 0
        }
    
    def training_step(
        self,
        batch: tuple,
        criterion: nn.Module
    ) -> Dict[str, float]:
        """
        Perform one training step with mixed precision.
        
        Args:
            batch: (inputs, targets) tuple
            criterion: Loss function
            
        Returns:
            Dictionary with loss and other metrics
        """
        inputs, targets = batch
        inputs = inputs.to(self.device)
        targets = targets.to(self.device)
        
        self.optimizer.zero_grad()
        
        # Forward pass with autocast
        with autocast(enabled=self.enabled):
            outputs = self.model(inputs)
            loss = criterion(outputs, targets)
        
        # Backward pass with gradient scaling
        self.scaler.scale(loss).backward()
        
        # Unscale gradients and clip if needed
        self.scaler.unscale_(self.optimizer)
        grad_norm = torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(
            self.model.parameters(),
            max_norm=1.0
        )
        
        # Optimizer step with scaler
        self.scaler.step(self.optimizer)
        
        # Update scaler
        old_scale = self.scaler.get_scale()
        self.scaler.update()
        new_scale = self.scaler.get_scale()
        
        # Track statistics
        self.stats['scale_history'].append(new_scale)
        self.stats['step_count'] += 1
        if new_scale < old_scale:
            self.stats['overflow_count'] += 1
        
        return {
            'loss': loss.item(),
            'grad_norm': grad_norm.item(),
            'scale': new_scale
        }
    
    def get_precision_stats(self) ->
```python
    def get_precision_stats(self) -> Dict[str, float]:
        """
        Get mixed precision training statistics.
        
        Returns:
            Dictionary with precision statistics
        """
        if len(self.stats['scale_history']) == 0:
            return {}
        
        return {
            'current_scale': self.stats['scale_history'][-1],
            'avg_scale': np.mean(self.stats['scale_history']),
            'overflow_rate': self.stats['overflow_count'] / max(self.stats['step_count'], 1),
            'total_steps': self.stats['step_count']
        }


class MixedPrecisionAwareModel(nn.Module):
    """
    Model designed to work well with mixed precision training.
    
    Key considerations:
    - Avoid operations that cause numerical instability in FP16
    - Use layer normalization instead of batch norm where possible
    - Careful initialization to prevent overflow/underflow
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        num_classes: int = 10,
        hidden_dim: int = 512,
        use_layer_norm: bool = True
    ):
        super().__init__()
        
        self.use_layer_norm = use_layer_norm
        
        # Feature extractor
        self.features = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(3, 64, 3, padding=1),
            self._get_norm_layer(64),
            nn.ReLU(),
            
            nn.Conv2d(64, 128, 3, padding=1),
            self._get_norm_layer(128),
            nn.ReLU(),
            
            nn.Conv2d(128, 256, 3, padding=1),
            self._get_norm_layer(256),
            nn.ReLU(),
            
            nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1)
        )
        
        # Classifier with careful design for FP16
        self.classifier = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(256, hidden_dim),
            nn.LayerNorm(hidden_dim) if use_layer_norm else nn.BatchNorm1d(hidden_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(0.5),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, num_classes)
        )
        
        self._initialize_for_mixed_precision()
    
    def _get_norm_layer(self, channels: int) -> nn.Module:
        """Get normalization layer suitable for mixed precision."""
        if self.use_layer_norm:
            # LayerNorm is more stable in FP16
            return nn.GroupNorm(32, channels)
        else:
            return nn.BatchNorm2d(channels)
    
    def _initialize_for_mixed_precision(self):
        """
        Initialize weights carefully for mixed precision.
        
        Use smaller initialization scale to prevent overflow in FP16.
        """
        for m in self.modules():
            if isinstance(m, nn.Conv2d):
                # Use smaller std for FP16 stability
                nn.init.kaiming_normal_(m.weight, mode='fan_out', nonlinearity='relu')
                if m.weight.data.abs().max() > 10:
                    m.weight.data = m.weight.data / 10
                if m.bias is not None:
                    nn.init.zeros_(m.bias)
                    
            elif isinstance(m, nn.Linear):
                nn.init.normal_(m.weight, 0, 0.01)
                if m.bias is not None:
                    nn.init.zeros_(m.bias)
                    
            elif isinstance(m, (nn.BatchNorm2d, nn.LayerNorm, nn.GroupNorm)):
                if hasattr(m, 'weight') and m.weight is not None:
                    nn.init.ones_(m.weight)
                if hasattr(m, 'bias') and m.bias is not None:
                    nn.init.zeros_(m.bias)
    
    def forward(self, x):
        """Forward pass with mixed precision considerations."""
        x = self.features(x)
        x = torch.flatten(x, 1)
        x = self.classifier(x)
        return x


class AdaptiveLossScaler:
    """
    Custom adaptive loss scaling for better mixed precision training.
    
    Dynamically adjusts loss scale based on gradient statistics.
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        init_scale: float = 2.**16,
        scale_factor: float = 2.0,
        scale_window: int = 2000,
        min_scale: float = 1.0,
        max_scale: float = 2.**24
    ):
        """
        Initialize adaptive loss scaler.
        
        Args:
            init_scale: Initial loss scale
            scale_factor: Factor to grow/shrink scale
            scale_window: Steps between scale adjustments
            min_scale: Minimum loss scale
            max_scale: Maximum loss scale
        """
        self.scale = init_scale
        self.scale_factor = scale_factor
        self.scale_window = scale_window
        self.min_scale = min_scale
        self.max_scale = max_scale
        
        self.growth_tracker = 0
        self.overflow_tracker = 0
    
    def update_scale(self, overflow: bool):
        """
        Update loss scale based on overflow detection.
        
        Args:
            overflow: Whether overflow was detected
        """
        if overflow:
            # Reduce scale on overflow
            self.scale = max(self.scale / self.scale_factor, self.min_scale)
            self.growth_tracker = 0
            self.overflow_tracker += 1
        else:
            # Increase scale if no overflow for scale_window steps
            self.growth_tracker += 1
            if self.growth_tracker >= self.scale_window:
                self.scale = min(self.scale * self.scale_factor, self.max_scale)
                self.growth_tracker = 0
    
    def get_scale(self) -> float:
        """Get current loss scale."""
        return self.scale


class MixedPrecisionOptimizer:
    """
    Wrapper for optimizer with mixed precision support and advanced features.
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        optimizer: torch.optim.Optimizer,
        loss_scaler: Optional[AdaptiveLossScaler] = None,
        clip_grad_norm: float = 1.0
    ):
        """
        Initialize mixed precision optimizer.
        
        Args:
            optimizer: Base optimizer
            loss_scaler: Custom loss scaler
            clip_grad_norm: Maximum gradient norm
        """
        self.optimizer = optimizer
        self.loss_scaler = loss_scaler or AdaptiveLossScaler()
        self.clip_grad_norm = clip_grad_norm
    
    def backward_and_step(
        self,
        loss: torch.Tensor,
        model: nn.Module
    ) -> Dict[str, float]:
        """
        Perform backward pass and optimizer step with loss scaling.
        
        Args:
            loss: Loss tensor
            model: Model being trained
            
        Returns:
            Dictionary with step statistics
        """
        # Scale loss
        scaled_loss = loss * self.loss_scaler.get_scale()
        
        # Backward pass
        scaled_loss.backward()
        
        # Check for overflow
        overflow = self._check_overflow(model)
        
        stats = {
            'loss': loss.item(),
            'scale': self.loss_scaler.get_scale(),
            'overflow': overflow
        }
        
        if not overflow:
            # Unscale gradients
            self._unscale_gradients(model)
            
            # Clip gradients
            grad_norm = torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(
                model.parameters(),
                self.clip_grad_norm
            )
            stats['grad_norm'] = grad_norm.item()
            
            # Optimizer step
            self.optimizer.step()
        
        # Update loss scale
        self.loss_scaler.update_scale(overflow)
        
        # Zero gradients
        self.optimizer.zero_grad()
        
        return stats
    
    def _check_overflow(self, model: nn.Module) -> bool:
        """Check if gradients have overflowed."""
        for param in model.parameters():
            if param.grad is not None:
                if not torch.isfinite(param.grad).all():
                    return True
        return False
    
    def _unscale_gradients(self, model: nn.Module):
        """Unscale gradients after backward pass."""
        inv_scale = 1.0 / self.loss_scaler.get_scale()
        for param in model.parameters():
            if param.grad is not None:
                param.grad.mul_(inv_scale)


# Example usage for mixed-precision training
def example_mixed_precision_training():
    """Complete example of mixed precision training."""
    
    print("Setting up mixed precision training...")
    
    # Check CUDA availability
    device = 'cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu'
    print(f"Using device: {device}")
    
    # Create model
    model = MixedPrecisionAwareModel(
        num_classes=10,
        hidden_dim=512,
        use_layer_norm=True
    )
    
    # Create optimizer
    optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW(
        model.parameters(),
        lr=0.001,
        weight_decay=0.01
    )
    
    # Create mixed precision trainer
    mp_trainer = MixedPrecisionTrainer(
        model=model,
        optimizer=optimizer,
        device=device,
        enabled=True
    )
    
    # Loss function
    criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
    
    # Dummy training data
    num_epochs = 5
    batch_size = 32
    
    print(f"\nTraining with mixed precision (FP16) enabled: {mp_trainer.enabled}")
    
    for epoch in range(num_epochs):
        epoch_loss = 0.0
        num_batches = 10
        
        for batch_idx in range(num_batches):
            # Generate dummy batch
            inputs = torch.randn(batch_size, 3, 32, 32)
            targets = torch.randint(0, 10, (batch_size,))
            batch = (inputs, targets)
            
            # Training step
            stats = mp_trainer.training_step(batch, criterion)
            epoch_loss += stats['loss']
            
            if batch_idx % 5 == 0:
                print(f"Epoch {epoch}, Batch {batch_idx}: "
                      f"Loss={stats['loss']:.4f}, "
                      f"GradNorm={stats['grad_norm']:.4f}, "
                      f"Scale={stats['scale']:.0f}")
        
        avg_loss = epoch_loss / num_batches
        print(f"Epoch {epoch} completed. Average Loss: {avg_loss:.4f}")
    
    # Get final statistics
    precision_stats = mp_trainer.get_precision_stats()
    print("\nMixed Precision Training Statistics:")
    print(f"  Current Scale: {precision_stats['current_scale']:.0f}")
    print(f"  Average Scale: {precision_stats['avg_scale']:.0f}")
    print(f"  Overflow Rate: {precision_stats['overflow_rate']:.4%}")
    print(f"  Total Steps: {precision_stats['total_steps']}")
    
    return model, mp_trainer


# Advanced: Dynamic precision switching
class DynamicPrecisionModel(nn.Module):
    """
    Model that can dynamically switch between precisions.
    
    Useful for training with FP16 and inference with INT8.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, num_classes: int = 10):
        super().__init__()
        
        self.features = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(3, 64, 3, padding=1),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(64, 128, 3, padding=1),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1)
        )
        
        self.classifier = nn.Linear(128, num_classes)
        
        # Precision mode
        self.precision_mode = 'fp32'  # 'fp32', 'fp16', 'int8'
    
    def set_precision(self, mode: str):
        """Set precision mode."""
        valid_modes = ['fp32', 'fp16', 'int8']
        if mode not in valid_modes:
            raise ValueError(f"Mode must be one of {valid_modes}")
        self.precision_mode = mode
    
    def forward(self, x):
        """Forward pass with dynamic precision."""
        if self.precision_mode == 'fp16':
            with autocast(enabled=True):
                x = self.features(x)
                x = torch.flatten(x, 1)
                x = self.classifier(x)
        else:
            x = self.features(x)
            x = torch.flatten(x, 1)
            x = self.classifier(x)
        
        return x

# Utility functions for compression analysis
class CompressionAnalyzer:
    """
    Comprehensive analyzer for model compression techniques.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, model: nn.Module):
        """
        Initialize compression analyzer.
        
        Args:
            model: Model to analyze
        """
        self.model = model
    
    def analyze_layer_sparsity(self) -> Dict[str, float]:
        """
        Analyze sparsity per layer.
        
        Returns:
            Dictionary mapping layer names to sparsity ratios
        """
        layer_sparsity = {}
        
        for name, module in self.model.named_modules():
            if isinstance(module, (nn.Conv2d, nn.Linear)):
                weight = module.weight.data
                zeros = (weight == 0).sum().item()
                total = weight.numel()
                sparsity = zeros / total if total > 0 else 0
                layer_sparsity[name] = sparsity
        
        return layer_sparsity
    
    def analyze_parameter_distribution(self) -> Dict[str, np.ndarray]:
        """
        Analyze parameter value distributions.
        
        Returns:
            Dictionary with distribution statistics
        """
        all_params = []
        
        for param in self.model.parameters():
            all_params.extend(param.data.cpu().numpy().flatten())
        
        all_params = np.array(all_params)
        
        return {
            'mean': np.mean(all_params),
            'std': np.std(all_params),
            'min': np.min(all_params),
            'max': np.max(all_params),
            'percentiles': np.percentile(all_params, [25, 50, 75, 95, 99])
        }
    
    def estimate_memory_footprint(
        self,
        precision: str = 'fp32',
        sparsity: float = 0.0
    ) -> Dict[str, float]:
        """
        Estimate memory footprint with different configurations.
        
        Args:
            precision: 'fp32', 'fp16', or 'int8'
            sparsity: Sparsity ratio (0.0 to 1.0)
            
        Returns:
            Dictionary with memory estimates
        """
        bytes_per_param = {
            'fp32': 4,
            'fp16': 2,
            'int8': 1
        }
        
        total_params = sum(p.numel() for p in self.model.parameters())
        active_params = total_params * (1 - sparsity)
        
        # Dense storage
        dense_memory = total_params * bytes_per_param[precision]
        
        # Sparse storage (CSR format overhead)
        if sparsity > 0:
            # Values + row indices + column pointers
            sparse_memory = (
                active_params * bytes_per_param[precision] +  # values
                active_params * 4 +  # column indices
                total_params * 4 / 1000  # row pointers (approximate)
            )
        else:
            sparse_memory = dense_memory
        
        return {
            'total_params': total_params,
            'active_params': int(active_params),
            'dense_memory_mb': dense_memory / 1024 / 1024,
            'sparse_memory_mb': sparse_memory / 1024 / 1024,
            'memory_saved_mb': (dense_memory - sparse_memory) / 1024 / 1024
        }
    
    def compare_configurations(self) -> None:
        """
        Compare different compression configurations.
        """
        print("\n" + "=" * 60)
        print("COMPRESSION CONFIGURATION COMPARISON")
        print("=" * 60)
        
        configs = [
            ('FP32 Dense', 'fp32', 0.0),
            ('FP16 Dense', 'fp16', 0.0),
            ('INT8 Dense', 'int8', 0.0),
            ('FP32 50% Sparse', 'fp32', 0.5),
            ('FP16 50% Sparse', 'fp16', 0.5),
            ('INT8 70% Sparse', 'int8', 0.7),
        ]
        
        baseline = None
        
        for name, precision, sparsity in configs:
            stats = self.estimate_memory_footprint(precision, sparsity)
            
            if baseline is None:
                baseline = stats['dense_memory_mb']
            
            compression_ratio = baseline / stats['sparse_memory_mb']
            
            print(f"\n{name}:")
            print(f"  Active params: {stats['active_params']:,}")
            print(f"  Memory: {stats['sparse_memory_mb']:.2f} MB")
            print(f"  Compression: {compression_ratio:.2f}x")


# Benchmark utilities
class CompressionBenchmark:
    """
    Benchmark compression techniques for speed and accuracy.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, device: str = 'cuda'):
        """
        Initialize benchmark.
        
        Args:
            device: Device for benchmarking
        """
        self.device = device if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu'
    
    def benchmark_inference_speed(
        self,
        model: nn.Module,
        input_shape: tuple = (1, 3, 224, 224),
        num_iterations: int = 100,
        warmup: int = 10
    ) -> Dict[str, float]:
        """
        Benchmark inference speed.
        
        Args:
            model: Model to benchmark
            input_shape: Input tensor shape
            num_iterations: Number of iterations
            warmup: Warmup iterations
            
        Returns:
            Dictionary with timing statistics
        """
        model = model.to(self.device)
        model.eval()
        
        dummy_input = torch.randn(*input_shape).to(self.device)
        
        # Warmup
        with torch.no_grad():
            for _ in range(warmup):
                _ = model(dummy_input)
        
        # Synchronize if using CUDA
        if self.device == 'cuda':
            torch.cuda.synchronize()
        
        # Benchmark
        import time
        times = []
        
        with torch.no_grad():
            for _ in range(num_iterations):
                start = time.perf_counter()
                _ = model(dummy_input)
                
                if self.device == 'cuda':
                    torch.cuda.synchronize()
                
                end = time.perf_counter()
                times.append(end - start)
        
        times = np.array(times) * 1000  # Convert to ms
        
        return {
            'mean_ms': np.mean(times),
            'std_ms': np.std(times),
            'min_ms': np.min(times),
            'max_ms': np.max(times),
            'median_ms': np.median(times),
            'throughput_fps': 1000 / np.mean(times)
        }
    
    def compare_model_variants(
        self,
        models: Dict[str, nn.Module],
        input_shape: tuple = (1, 3, 224, 224)
    ) -> None:
        """
        Compare different model variants.
        
        Args:
            models: Dictionary of model name to model
            input_shape: Input shape for benchmarking
        """
        print("\n" + "=" * 60)
        print("MODEL VARIANT COMPARISON")
        print("=" * 60)
        
        results = {}
        
        for name, model in models.items():
            print(f"\nBenchmarking {name}...")
            stats = self.benchmark_inference_speed(model, input_shape)
            
            param_count = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())
            
            results[name] = {
                'params': param_count,
                'latency_ms': stats['mean_ms'],
                'throughput_fps': stats['throughput_fps']
            }
            
            print(f"  Parameters: {param_count:,}")
            print(f"  Latency: {stats['mean_ms']:.2f} ± {stats['std_ms']:.2f} ms")
            print(f"  Throughput: {stats['throughput_fps']:.1f} FPS")
        
        # Print comparison table
        if len(results) > 1:
            print("\n" + "-" * 60)
            print("Relative Performance (vs first model):")
            print("-" * 60)
            
            baseline_name = list(results.keys())[0]
            baseline = results[baseline_name]
            
            for name, stats in results.items():
                if name == baseline_name:
                    continue
                
                param_ratio = baseline['params'] / stats['params']
                speedup = baseline['latency_ms'] / stats['latency_ms']
                
                print(f"\n{name} vs {baseline_name}:")
                print(f"  Parameter reduction: {param_ratio:.2f}x")
                print(f"  Speedup: {speedup:.2f}x")


# Main execution examples
if __name__ == "__main__":

## Summary and Best Practices

```python
"""
COMPRESSION-AWARE TRAINING PATTERNS - SUMMARY
==============================================

1. QUANTIZATION-AWARE TRAINING (QAT)
   - Simulates quantization during training
   - Learns quantization-robust parameters
   - Best for: Deployment on edge devices, mobile
   - Typical compression: 4x (FP32 -> INT8)

2. PRUNING-AWARE TRAINING
   - Gradually removes unimportant weights
   - Model adapts to sparsity during training
   - Best for: Reducing model size and computation
   - Typical compression: 2-10x depending on sparsity

3. COMPRESSION-FRIENDLY ARCHITECTURE
   - Designs models inherently efficient
   - Uses depthwise separable convolutions
   - Best for: New model development
   - Typical compression: 3-5x vs standard architectures

4. MIXED-PRECISION TRAINING
   - Uses FP16 for speed, FP32 for stability
   - Reduces memory and speeds up training
   - Best for: Large models, GPU training
   - Typical speedup: 2-3x on modern GPUs

COMBINING TECHNIQUES:
- Start with compression-friendly architecture
- Train with mixed precision for efficiency
- Apply pruning during/after training
- Finish with quantization-aware fine-tuning
- Potential total compression: 10-50x

KEY CONSIDERATIONS:
- Always validate accuracy after compression
- Use gradual compression schedules
- Monitor for numerical instability
- Benchmark on target hardware
- Consider accuracy vs efficiency tradeoffs
"""
